*Gloss, mine and tentative:* "The wise knew the form of the delightful one when the hawk brought the *andhas* from afar. — Whom the well-winged son of the hawk brought from afar."

"The chief part of this story is described in the form of a dialogue in the 26th and 27th sūktas of the fourth maṇḍala of the Ṛksaṃhitā. But since the different words *śyena*, *suparṇa* and *gāyatrī* are used in these contexts, these contexts become meaningful only after one has learnt the details of this story."

"In explaining this Ṛk, Skandasvāmin cites the story told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. According to it (Ai. Brā. 3-25 [read: 3-[?]] to 3-26 [?]), the ṛṣis, wishing to obtain Soma, who was in the world of heaven, as king, prayed to the Chandas — the metres — to bring that King Soma to them. Then they agreed, and, because this work was accomplished by a change into the form of a *suparṇa* [bird], this episode is well known as the *Sauparṇākhyāna*. Thereupon, in the form of birds, the metres exerted themselves; but because the Jagatī, going by the way, fell short [lit.: gave out] in the middle of the road, the Triṣṭubh metre was sent out. This too —

---

### Page 492 (PDF 507)

*(Running head: left "492", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 14 Sū. 93".)*

"— was unable to complete the way, going beyond the half-way, and had to return. Then the Gāyatrī flew upward, and, having terrified the Soma-guards, seized Soma with her beak and her feet. Then one of the Soma-guards, Kṛśānu, shot an arrow, and it cut off one claw of this bird. Even so the Gāyatrī accomplished her task. The part that she held in her right foot became the *prātaḥsavana*, the part in her left foot the *mādhyandinasavana*, and the part in her beak the *tṛtīyasavana*."

"In the same way, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too (1-7-2-10 [?]) it is said: '*tad dvai kaniṣṭhaṃ chandaḥ sad gāyatrī prathamā chandasāṃ yujyate tad tad dvir erkyaiva yajñair eno bhūtvā divaḥ somam ābharat*' [as read, clotted [?]] — in the Chandas, though the Gāyatrī is the smallest in the number of syllables, she attains the first place of all the metres. By her own power, taking the form of a hawk, she brought Soma from the world of the gods. At the time of the oblations too the praise of the Gāyatrī as a hawk is well known (Śat. Brā. 3-4-1-13 [?]; 3-9-4-10 [?]). In this very context the point that Agni and Gāyatrī are the same in nature, [as in] '*agnir vai gāyatrī tad gāyatry etam imam īte sā yad gāyatrī śyeno bhūtvā*', will be explained later."

"This same narrative, with a little change, is found in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6-1 [?]): once, there was a wager between Kadrū and Suparṇī; since Kadrū won, Suparṇī had to become her servant. Then Kadrū said to Suparṇī, 'bring Soma from the mid-region, disguised as a thief, and give him as the ransom, then you will be freed.' Then Suparṇī, to seek the help of her children, the metres, [commissioned them]; the efforts of the Jagatī and the Triṣṭubh both failed, and the Gāyatrī accomplished the work: so runs the story of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā."

***brahmaṇā vavṛdhānā*** — "Since *andhaḥ, vājaḥ, payaḥ* and the like are read among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 [?]), here it can be 'by food in the form of oblation'; or else, since the word *brahman* is explained as 'work' or as 'mantra' (Ni. 3-[?] [?]), the meaning may be 'by rites such as sacrifice or by mantras': 'having obtained increase by these'. Or, since the root *vṛdh* is generally used in the Ṛksaṃhitā in the sense 'praise' [*praśaṃsā*], it may also be 'those who have been praised'."

***yajñāya uru lokaṃ cakrathuḥ*** — "'You made a broad place of sacrifice for the sacrifice performed with reference to the other deities': this is the meaning."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.6)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*jabhāra* — root *hṛñ haraṇe* [as printed for *bhṛñ*? — the print gives *hṛñ*, with the Vedic *h→bh* by the rule cited below [?]]; *liṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; by *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…* (Pā. 3-4-82 [?]) the replacement *ṇal*; the root is doubled; the reduplicative takes *ur at*; *cutva*; by *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pā. 7-2-116 [?]) the vṛddhi of the penultimate; by *hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi* [vārttika] the replacement *bha* for *ha*; since it follows a word, the *nighāta* accent.
*amathnāt* — root *mantha viloḍane*; *laṅ*, third person singular; by *itaś ca* the *i* is elided; by *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* the stem-suffix *śnā*; by *sārvadhātukam apit* (Pā. 1-2-4 [?]) it is treated as *ṅit*; by *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* (Pā. 6-4-24 [?]) the nasal of the penultimate is elided; the augment *aṭ*; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*; since the augment is acute, the word is initial-acute.
*vavṛdhānā* — root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; in it, *liṭ*; by *liṭaḥ kānajvā* (Pā. 3-2-106 [?]) the suffix *kānac*; the root is doubled because of it; in the reduplicative *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; *ur at*; again *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ*; since *kānac* is *kit*, the guṇa of the light penultimate of the root does not occur; by the Vedic usage the reduplicative is lengthened; the dual ending *au* follows, and by *supāṃ sulug* it is replaced by *ā*. ‖ 6 ‖

*agnīṣomā | haviṣaḥ | pra-sthitasya | vītam | haryatam | vṛṣaṇā | juṣethām | su-śarmāṇā | su-avasā | hi | bhūtam | atha | dhattam | yajamānāya | śam | yoḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 93.7)**

> हे अग्नीषोमौ प्रस्थितस्य होमार्थमाहवनीयसमीपं प्राप्तं हविष इदं हविर्वीतं भक्षयतं । तदनन्तरं च हर्यतं । अस्मान्कामयेथां । हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारौ जुषेथां । अस्मदीयं परिचरणं सेवेथां । तदनन्तरं सुशर्माणा शोभनसुखौ स्ववसा हि शोभनरक्षणौ च भूतं । अस्माकं भवतं । अथानन्तरं हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय शं शमनीयानां रोगाणां शमनं योः पृथक्कर्तव्यानां भयानां यावनं पृथक्करणं च धत्तं । विधत्तं । कुरुतं । उक्तं च यास्केन । शमनं च रोगाणां यावनं च भयानां । नि. ४-२१ [?] । इति ॥ हविषः । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी । वीतं । वी गतिप्रजनकान्त्यसनखादनेषु । ह्यसस्तं [clotted [?]] । आदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । वीतं च हर्यतं चेति चार्थप्रतीतेश्चादिलोपे विभाषेति प्रथमायास्त्रिज्विभक्तेर्निघातप्रतिषेधः । हर्यतं । पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । जुषेथां । वृषणेत्यामन्त्रितस्यामन्त्रितं पूर्वमिति तिङः परत्वान्निघाताभावः । सुशर्माणा स्ववसा । उभयत्र बहुव्रीहौ सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । भूतं । लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् ॥

*he agnīṣomau prasthitasya homārtham āhavanīyasamīpaṃ prāptaṃ haviṣa idaṃ havir vītaṃ bhakṣayataṃ | tadanantaraṃ ca haryataṃ | asmān kāmayethāṃ | he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārau juṣethāṃ | asmadīyaṃ paricaraṇaṃ sevethāṃ | tadanantaraṃ suśarmāṇā śobhanasukhau svavasā hi śobhanarakṣaṇau ca bhūtaṃ | asmākaṃ bhavataṃ | athānantaraṃ havirdattavate yajamānāya śaṃ śamanīyānāṃ rogāṇāṃ śamanaṃ yoḥ pṛthakkartavyānāṃ bhayānāṃ yāvanaṃ pṛthakkaraṇaṃ ca dhattaṃ | vidhattaṃ | kurutaṃ | uktaṃ ca yāskena | śamanaṃ ca rogāṇāṃ yāvanaṃ ca bhayānām | Ni. 4-21 [?] | iti ‖ haviṣaḥ | kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam iti karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvāc caturthyarthe ṣaṣṭhī | vītaṃ | vī gatiprajanakāntyasanakhādaneṣu | hy asastaṃ [clotted [?]] | ādāditvāc chapo luk | vītaṃ ca haryataṃ ceti cārthapratīteś cādilope vibhāṣeti prathamāyās trijvibhakter nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | haryataṃ | pādāditvān nighātābhāvaḥ | juṣethāṃ | vṛṣaṇety āmantritasyāmantritaṃ pūrvam iti tiṅaḥ paratvān nighātābhāvaḥ | suśarmāṇā svavasā | ubhayatra bahuvrīhau sor manasī alomoṣasī ity uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | bhūtaṃ | loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni and Soma, *haviṣaḥ prasthitasya* — of the oblation set forth, brought near the Āhavanīya fire for the offering — *vītam*, eat this oblation; and thereafter *haryatam*, desire us. O *vṛṣaṇā*, showerers of desires, *juṣethām*, accept our service. Thereafter be *suśarmāṇā*, of good happiness, and *svavasā*, of good protection, for us. Then *dhattam*, grant to the sacrificer who has given the oblation *śam* — the quieting of the diseases to be quieted — and *yoḥ* — the keeping apart of the fears to be kept apart. So Yāska says: 'quieting of diseases and keeping off of fears' (Ni. 4-21 [?])."

*Grammar tail (partly clotted; characterized):* *haviṣaḥ* — the genitive stands for the dative, since the object is a recipient (*kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam*). *vītam* — root *vī* of the *adādi* class; *luk* of *śap*; the *nighāta* prohibited by the connexion of *vītaṃ ca haryataṃ ca*. *haryatam* — at the head of the pāda, no *nighāta*. *juṣethām* — since the vocative *vṛṣaṇā* stands before, no *nighāta*. *suśarmāṇā svavasā* — in both *bahuvrīhis*, the final member's initial-acute by *sor manasī alomoṣasī*.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 93.7)** *(Kannada; continues on p. 495)*

*agnīṣomā* — O Agni and Soma deities; *prasthitasya* — (placed in the Āhavanīya fire) offered; *haviṣaḥ* — the oblation; *vītam* — eat; *haryatam* — be gracious to us (or: desire this oblation and eat it); *vṛṣaṇā* — you who shower desired things; *juṣethām* — accept (our service) and take pleasure; *suśarmāṇā* — givers of excellent happiness; *svavasā hi* — and givers of excellent protection; *bhūtam* — be (to us); *atha* — thereafter; *yajamānāya* —

*(Pratipadārtha, concluded:)* "— to the sacrificer; *śam* — happiness free of disease; *yoḥ* — happiness in the form of freedom from fear; *dhattam* — bring about."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 93.7** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni and Soma deities, eat our oblations offered in the Āhavanīya fire. Being gracious to us and showering our desired ends, accept our services, and be to us givers of excellent happiness and of excellent protection; and bring about for the sacrificer who offers oblations happiness free of disease and free of fear."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 93.7)*

"Agni and Soma, partake of the proffered oblations ; be gracious to us ; showerers of desires, be pleased ; prosperous and deligent [sic] protectors, be propitious and grant to the sacrificer health exemption from ill." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 93.7)** *(Kannada)*

***prasthitasya*** — "'Placed in the Āhavanīya fire': that is, offered in it."

***vītam*** — "*vītam* — *aśnītam* (Ni. 4-[?] [?]): eat."

***śaṃyoḥ*** — *sukhaṃ yoḥ* (Ni. 4-21 [?]) *śamanaṃ ca rogāṇāṃ yāvanaṃ ca bhayānām* | "That is, happiness in the form of quieting of diseases and happiness in the form of warding off fear: 'quiet our diseases and ward off fear' is the idea. In *tac chaṃyor āvṛṇīmahe* (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-10-2 [?]) *śaṃyu* means 'son of Bṛhaspati', but here it only means 'giver of happiness'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.7)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*haviṣaḥ* — in the sūtra laying down the name *saṃpradāna*, the statement "*kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyam*" gives the name *saṃpradāna* to the object, so the genitive stands in the sense of the dative.
*vītam* — root *vī gatiprajanakāntyasanakhādaneṣu*, *adādi*; *loṭ*, second person dual; by *tas thas thamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ* the replacement *tam*; by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* the *luk* of *śap*; when connecting *vītaṃ ca haryataṃ ca*, the sense of *ca* is evident, and by *cādilope vibhāṣā* (Pā. 8-1-63 [?]) the prohibition of *nighāta* for a verb standing first applies; the final-acute by the suffix accent.

### Page 496 (PDF 511)

*(Running head: left "496", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 14 Sū. 93".)*

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 93.7, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly):*

*haryatam* — root *harya gatikāntyoḥ*, *bhvādi*; *kānti* means 'wish'; as before, *loṭ* second person dual; since it stands at the head of the pāda, no *nighāta*; *śap* is unaccented as it is *pit*; the *lasārvadhātuka* after the *udāttopadeśa* root is unaccented by *tāsyanudāttetṅ…*; the accent of the root remains.
*vṛṣaṇā* — the nominative dual *au*, by *supāṃ sulug* replaced by *ā*; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the lengthening of the penultimate does not occur.
*juṣethām* — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*, *ātmanepada* since it is *anudāttet*; *loṭ*, second person dual; since the vocative *vṛṣaṇā* stands before, it counts as non-existent (*āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat*), and since a verb precedes … by *atiṅaḥ* the *nighāta* does not occur; by the suffix accent the middle syllable is acute.
*suśarmāṇā, svavasā* — both are *bahuvrīhis*, ending in *man* and *as*; by *sor manasī alomoṣasī* the final member's initial-acute.
*bhūtam* — root *bhū sattāyām*; *loṭ*, second person dual; the replacement *tam*; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the *luk* of *śap*; since *tam* is *pit* by the rule *sārvadhātukam apit*, the *guṇa* of the root vowel does not occur; since *hi* ("for") is connected, by *hicca* (Pā. 8-1-34 [?]) the *nighāta* is prohibited, and by the suffix accent the final-acute. ‖ 7 ‖

*yaḥ | agnīṣomā | haviṣā | saparyāt | devadrīcā | manasā | yaḥ | ghṛtena | tasya | vratam | rakṣatam | pātam | aṃhasaḥ | viśe | janāya | mahi | śarma | yacchatam ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 93.8)**

> यो यजमानोऽग्निषोमौ [sic: *agnīṣomau*] हे अग्नीषोमौ देवद्रीचा देवानञ्चता देवतापरायणेन श्रद्धायुक्तेन मनसान्तःकरणेन युक्तः सन् हविषा चरुपुरोडाशादिना सपर्यात् सपर्यति परिचरति । यश्च यजमानो घृतेनाज्येनाग्नीषोमौ परिचरिति । तस्य यजमानस्य व्रतं कर्म रक्षतम् । अंहसः पापात्तं च यजमानं पातम् । रक्षतम् । विशे योगेषु प्रविशते तस्मै जनाय यजमानाय महि महत्त्वभूतं शर्म सुखं यच्छतं । दत्तम् ॥ अग्नीषोमा । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सपर्यात् । सपर पूजायां । कण्ड्वादिः । लेट्यडागमः । देवद्रीचा । सेवानाञ्चतीति सेवद्र्यञ्च् । अञ्चतेर्ऋत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । अनिदितामिति नलोपः । विष्वग्देवयोश्च टेरद्र्यञ्चतावप्रत्यये । पा. ६-३-९२ [?] । इति देवशब्दस्य टेरद्र्यादेशः । तृतीयैकवचने टाच् [?] इत्याकारलोपे चावितीति दीर्घत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते द्रिसथ्योरन्तोदात्तनिपातनं कृत्स्वरनिवृत्त्यर्थं । पा. ६-२-५३-१ [?] इति वचनाद्द्र्यादेशोऽन्तोदात्तः । विशे । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

*yo yajamāno 'gnīṣomau he agnīṣomau devadrīcā devān añcatā devatāparāyaṇena śraddhāyuktena manasāntaḥkaraṇena yuktaḥ san haviṣā carupuroḍāśādinā saparyāt saparyati paricarati | yaś ca yajamāno ghṛtenājyenāgnīṣomau paricariti | tasya yajamānasya vrataṃ karma rakṣatam | aṃhasaḥ pāpāt taṃ ca yajamānaṃ pātam | rakṣatam | viśe yogeṣu praviśate tasmai janāya yajamānāya mahi mahattvabhūtaṃ śarma sukhaṃ yacchataṃ | dattam ‖ agnīṣomā | devatādvandve cety ubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | saparyāt | sapara pūjāyāṃ | kaṇḍvādiḥ | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | devadrīcā | sevānāñcatīti sevadryañc | añcater ṛtvigity ādinā kvin | aniditām iti nalopaḥ | viṣvagdevayoś ca ṭer adryañcatāv apratyaye | Pā. 6-3-92 [?] | iti devaśabdasya ṭer adryādeśaḥ | tṛtīyaikavacane ṭāc [?] ity ākāralope cāvīti dīrghatvaṃ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte drisathyor antodāttanipātanaṃ kṛtsvaranivṛttyarthaṃ | Pā. 6-2-53-1 [?] iti vacanād dryādeśo 'ntodāttaḥ | viśe | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ ‖*

*Translation:* "The sacrificer who, O Agni and Soma, *devadrīcā*, with a mind that goes towards the gods, devoted to the deities and endowed with faith, *saparyāt*, serves you with an oblation such as *caru* or *puroḍāśa*; and the sacrificer who serves Agni and Soma with ghee: *tasya vratam rakṣatam* — protect that sacrificer's rite; *pātam aṃhasaḥ* — protect him from sin. *Viśe janāya* — to the man who enters upon the rites, to the sacrificer, *yacchatam*, give *mahi śarma*, great happiness."

*Grammar tail (partly clotted):* *agnīṣomā* — in a deity-*dvandva* the natural accent of both members. *saparyāt* — root *sapara pūjāyām* of the *kaṇḍvādi* group; the augment *aṭ* in the *leṭ*. *devadrīcā* — "the one who goes to the gods": *devadryañc*; *kvin* after *añc*; the *n* elided; *devadryañc* by the rule *viṣvagdevayoś ca ṭer adryañcatāv apratyaye* (Pā. 6-3-92 [?]); the lengthening in the instrumental; the final-acute of *dri* by an irregular rule against the *kṛt* accent. *viśe* — the case-ending acute by *sāvekācas…*.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 93.8** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni and Soma deities, protect all the rites of every sacrificer who, with extreme faith and devotion to the gods, worships with *caru*, *puroḍāśa* and the like, and of the one who worships the deities with the oblation of ghee, and free them from sin. To the sacrificer who has entered the sacrificial rites give abundant happiness."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 93.8)*

"Agni and Soma, protect his sacrifice and defend him from ill, who with a mind devoted to the gods, worships you with clarified butter and oblations ; grant to the man engaged in devotion extreme happiness." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 93.8)** *(Kannada)*

***devadrīcā*** — *devān añcatā devatāparāyaṇena śraddhāyuktena* | "'With a mind of one wholly devoted to the deities': that is, with a mind that, having faith and devotion only to the deities, is intent on their service and attaches itself solely to them."

***vrataṃ rakṣatam*** — "Protect the rites such as sacrifice from the harm of the asuras, so that the sacrifice is brought to fulfilment."

***pātam aṃhasaḥ*** — "Many kinds of defects, whether in the sacrifice or at other times, are all sinful deeds; the sense is: save the sacrificer from such defects that may befall him beyond his own control, and free him from sin. Since the fear of sin is great in sacrificers, there are many examples of praying to Agni and Soma in this manner at every step —"

> यच्चिद्धि ते पुरुषत्रा यविष्ठाचित्तिभिश्चकृमा कच्चिदागः ।
> कृधी ष्वस्माँ अदितेरनागान्व्येनांसि शिश्रथो विष्वगग्ने ॥

*yac cid dhi te puruṣatrā yaviṣṭhācittibhiś cakṛmā kac cid āgaḥ | kṛdhī ṣv asmām̐ aditer anāgān vy enāṃsi śiśratho viṣvag agne ‖*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-12-4 [?]; numerals as read, doubtful)

***viśe janāya*** — "Here there is room for two meanings. Sāyaṇa explains: *viśe yogeṣu praviśate | janāya yajamānāya* — 'to the sacrificer who, having entered the sacrificial acts, worships the deities, give [happiness]'. Skandasvāmin explains: *viśe | manuṣyanāmaitat | putrādimanuṣyajātasvabhūtāya yajamānāya* — 'since *viś* is read among the names of men, *manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ, dhanāḥ* and the like (Ni. 2-2 [?]), *viśe* means 'to the sacrificer who has men — sons, grandsons and the rest — in his household'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.8)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*agnīṣomā* — by *supāṃ sulug* the dual ending is replaced by *ā*; by *devatādvandve ca* (Pā. 6-2-141 [?]) the natural accent of both members.
*saparyāt* — root *sapara pūjāyām*, of the *kaṇḍvādi* group; *leṭ*, third person singular; the *i* of *tip* is elided by *itaś ca lopaḥ*; by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* the augment *aṭ*; by *kaṇḍvādibhyo yak* (Pā. 3-1-27 [?]) *yak* in its own sense; by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* the stem is a root, so the *leṭ* is spoken of afterwards; since *yaḥ* is connected, no *nighāta*; the accent of *yak* remains.
*devadrīcā* — "*devān añcati iti devadryañc*"; root *añcu gatipūjanayoḥ*; when *deva* is the *upapada*, by *ṛtvigdadhṛk…* the suffix *kvin*; by *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ* the nasal of the penultimate is elided; since the root *añc* stands after it without a suffix, by *viṣvagdevayoś ca ṭer adryañcatāv apratyaye* (Pā. 6-3-92 [?]) *adri* for the *ṭi* of *deva*; the instrumental singular takes *ṭā*; when *devadri + añc + ā* stands, by *aco 'ñcaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-138 [?]) the *a* of the root is elided; by *cau* (Pā. 6-3-138 [?]) the preceding vowel is lengthened since the *añc* whose nasal is lost follows: *devadrī*; hence *devadrīcā*. By *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* the *kṛdanta* final member would keep its accent, but by *adrisathyor…antodāttanipātanam* [as read, clotted [?]] the irregular final-acute —

### Page 501 (PDF 516)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 33 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 501.)*

*Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Rik 93.9, concluded:*

> देवत्रा देवेषु सर्वेषु यौ युवां सं बभूवथुः । संभूतौ संभावितौ प्रशस्तौ स्थः । राजानौ वा एतौ देवतानां यदग्नीषोमाविति श्रुतेः ॥ सवेदसा । समानं वेदो ययोः । समानस्य छन्दसीति सभावः । वनतं । वन षण संभक्तौ । देवत्रा । देवमनुष्यपुरुषपुरुमर्त्येत्यादिना सप्तम्यर्थे त्राप्रत्ययः ॥

*devatrā deveṣu sarveṣu yau yuvāṃ saṃ babhūvathuḥ | saṃbhūtau saṃbhāvitau praśastau sthaḥ | rājānau vā etau devatānāṃ yad agnīṣomāv iti śruteḥ ‖ savedasā | samānaṃ vedo yayoḥ | samānasya chandasīti sabhāvaḥ | vanataṃ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | devatrā | devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyety ādinā saptamyarthe trāpratyayaḥ ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni and Soma, you two, *savedasā*, being endowed with one and the same *vedas*, wealth in the form of oblation, and *sahūtī*, having the same invocation: *vanatam*, accept our praises (*giraḥ*). *Devatrā*, among all the gods, you two *saṃ babhūvathuḥ* — are well-regarded, honoured, praised. 'These two, Agni and Soma, are the kings of the deities', says the śruti."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 93.9)** *(Kannada)*

*agnīṣomā* — O Agni and Soma deities; *savedasā* — possessed of one and the same kind of wealth (in the form of oblation); *sahūtī* — possessed of one and the same kind of invocation; *giraḥ* — our praise-words; *vanatam* — accept and enjoy; *devatrā* — among the deities; *saṃ babhūvathuḥ* — you have become exceedingly honoured.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 93.9** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni and Soma deities, one and the same kind of oblation is offered to both of you, and there is one and the same kind of invocation. Accept and enjoy together our praise-words. You two are exceedingly worthy of honour among all the deities."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 93.9)*

"Agni and Soma, endowed with the like wealth, and invoked by a common invocation, share our praises, for you have ever been the chief of the Gods." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 93.9)** *(Kannada)*

"In the sacrifice connected with Agni and Soma in the Paurṇamāsyeṣṭi, the Ṛk *agnīṣomā savedasā* is to be used as the *puronuvākyā* mantra; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra shows this, in the section *uktā devatā*, by the sūtra '*agnīṣomā savedasā yuvam etāni divi rocanāni*' (Ā. 1-6 [?])."

***giraḥ*** — *stutayo giraḥ gṛṇāteḥ* (Ni. 1-11 [?]) | "As explained earlier, *giraḥ* here means praises."

***vanatam*** — "*vaṣṭi, uśmasi* and the like being read among the words of wishing (Ni. 2-6 [?]), the sense is 'wish, desire': accept and enjoy our praises with regard."

***devatrā saṃ babhūvathuḥ*** — *sarveṣu deveṣu yuvāṃ saṃbhāvitau praśastau sthaḥ* | "Sāyaṇa explains that you two are the most worthy of honour among all the deities. But Skandasvāmin has explained, 'in all the deities together, you are sharers of the *puroḍāśa* oblation'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.9)** *(Kannada; the page continues on p. 502)*

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 93.9 (grammar page, noted briefly; its heading stands at the foot of p. 501):*

*savedasā* — "*samānaṃ vedo yayos tau savedasau*"; by *samānasya chandasi…* (Pā. 6-3-84 [?]) the replacement *sa* for *samāna*; the dual ending *au*, by *supāṃ sulug*, replaced by *ā*.
*sahūtī* — "*samānā hūtir yayos tau*"; as before the replacement *sa*; a dual.
*vanatam* — root *vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*; *loṭ*, second person dual; since it follows a word, the *nighāta* accent.
*devatrā* — after the word *deva*, in the sense of the locative, by *devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamyor bahulam* (Pā. 5-4-56 [?]) the suffix *trā*; by the suffix accent the final-acute. ‖ 9 ‖

> अग्नीषोमावनेन वां यो वां घृतेन दाशति ।

*agnīṣomāv anena vāṃ yo vāṃ ghṛtena dāśati | tasmai dīdayataṃ bṛhat ‖ 10 ‖*

### Page 503 (PDF 518)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 33 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 503.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 93.10)**

> हे अग्नीषोमौ वां युवयोः संबन्धी यो यजमानोऽनेन घृतेनोत्पवनादिभिः संस्कृतेनाज्येन युक्तं हविर्वां युवाभ्यां दाशति प्रयच्छति तस्मै यजमानाय बृहत्प्रभूतं धनं दीदयतं । प्रकाशयतं । प्रयच्छतमित्यर्थः ॥ दाशति । दाश्र दाने । शप्तिपोः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघातः । दीदयतं । दीदयतिर्दीप्त्यर्थः ॥

*he agnīṣomau vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhī yo yajamāno 'nena ghṛtenotpavanādibhiḥ saṃskṛtenājyena yuktaṃ havir vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ dāśati prayacchati tasmai yajamānāya bṛhat prabhūtaṃ dhanaṃ dīdayataṃ | prakāśayataṃ | prayacchatam ity arthaḥ ‖ dāśati | dāśra dāne | śaptipoḥ pittvād anudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | yadvṛttayogān nighātaḥ | dīdayataṃ | dīdayatir dīptyarthaḥ ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni and Soma, the sacrificer who, belonging to you two, *dāśati* — gives — *anena ghṛtena*, with this ghee (ghee purified by *utpavana* and the like), an oblation joined with it, to you: to that sacrificer *dīdayatam* — make shine, give — *bṛhat*, abundant wealth."

*Grammar tail:* *dāśati* — root *dāśṛ dāne*; since *śap* and *tip* are *pit* and unaccented, the accent of the root remains; the *nighāta* prevented by connexion with *yaḥ*. *dīdayatam* — *dīdayati* has the sense of shining.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 93.10)** *(Kannada)*

*agnīṣomā* — O Agni and Soma deities; *vām* — belonging to both of you; *yaḥ* — whichever sacrificer; *anena ghṛtena* — with this oblation of ghee; *vām* — to you; *dāśati* — offers the oblation; *tasmai* — to that sacrificer; *bṛhat* — abundant wealth; *dīdayatam* — give.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 93.10** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni and Soma deities, give abundant wealth to the sacrificer who offers to both of you the oblation together with this oblation of ghee."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 93.10)*

"Agni and Soma, give ample recompense to him who presents to you both, this clarified butter." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 93.10)** *(Kannada)*

***ghṛtena*** — "That is, an oblation together with ghee purified by *utpavana* and the like."

***dīdayatam*** — "*bhrājate, bhrāśate* and the like being read among the names of acts of shining (Ni. 2-[?] [?]), here the meaning is 'cause the abundant wealth to shine', that is, 'give it'. Mādhava explains *vardhayatam*: 'make it increase'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.10)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*dāśati* — root *dāśṛ dāne*; *laṭ*, third person singular; since *śap* is *pit*, and *tip* likewise unaccented, the accent of the root remains; because *yaḥ* precedes, by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. 8-1-66 [?]) the *nighāta* is prohibited.
*dīdayatam* — the root *dīdaya* has the sense of shining; *loṭ*, second person dual; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*. ‖ 10 ‖

### Page 504 (PDF 519)

*(Running head: left "504", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 14 Sū. 93".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 93.11)** *(Gāyatrī)*

> अग्नीषोमाविमानि नो युवं हव्या जुजोषतम् ।
> आ यातमुप नः सचा ॥ ११ ॥

*agnīṣomāv imāni no yuvaṃ havyā jujoṣatam | ā yātam upa naḥ sacā ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 93.11)**

> अग्नीषोमौ । इमानि । नः । युवम् । हव्या । जुजोषतम् ।
> आ । यातम् । उप । नः । सचा ॥ ११ ॥

*agnīṣomau | imāni | naḥ | yuvam | havyā | jujoṣatam | ā | yātam | upa | naḥ | sacā ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 93.11)**

> हे अग्नीषोमौ युवं युवां नोऽस्मदीयानीमानि हव्या हवींषि जुजोषतं । सेवेथां । तदर्थं नोऽस्मान् सचा सह युवामुपा यातं । उपागच्छतं ॥ जुजोषतं । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । लोटि व्यत्ययेन शप् । छान्दसं द्विर्वचनं । यद्वा । विकरणस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति श्लुः । ततो व्यत्ययेन शप् । बहुलं छन्दसीति वक्तव्यमिति वचनान्नाभ्यस्तस्याचि पितीति लघूपधगुणप्रतिषेधाभावः ॥

*he agnīṣomau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ no 'smadīyānīmāni havyā havīṃṣi jujoṣataṃ | sevethāṃ | tadarthaṃ no 'smān sacā saha yuvām upā yātaṃ | upāgacchataṃ ‖ jujoṣataṃ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | loṭi vyatyayena śap | chāndasaṃ dvirvacanaṃ | yadvā | vikaraṇasya bahulaṃ chandasīti śluḥ | tato vyatyayena śap | bahulaṃ chandasīti vaktavyam iti vacanān nābhyastasyāci pitīti laghūpadhaguṇapratiṣedhābhāvaḥ ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni and Soma, *yuvam*, you two, *jujoṣatam*, enjoy these our oblations. For that purpose come *upa*, towards us, *sacā*, together."

*Grammar tail:* *jujoṣatam* — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*; in the *loṭ*, *śap* by *vyatyaya*; the doubling is Vedic. Or: *ślu* for the stem-suffix by *bahulaṃ chandasi*, then *śap* by *vyatyaya*; by the statement "*bahulaṃ chandasīti vaktavyam*" the prohibition of the *guṇa* of the light penultimate by *nābhyastasyāci piti* does not apply.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 93.11)** *(Kannada)*

*agnīṣomā* — O Agni and Soma deities; *yuvam* — both of you together; *naḥ* — our; *imāni havyā* — these oblations; *jujoṣatam* — (in order to) enjoy; *naḥ* — fixing your eyes on us; *sacā* — both together; *upa ā yātam* — come, joining [us].

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 93.11** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni and Soma deities, both of you come together with company, to our place of sacrifice, in order to enjoy these our oblations."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 93.11)*

"Agni and Soma, be pleased with these our oblations and come to us together." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 93.11)** *(Kannada)*

***havyā*** — *havīṃṣi* | "Oblations; a word in the accusative plural."

***sacā*** — *saha* | "'Both of you come together (joining)': this is the meaning."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.11)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*havyā* — in the neuter plural the replacement *śi* came; by *śeś chandasi bahulam* the elision of *śi*.
*jujoṣatam* — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*; *loṭ*, second person dual; the replacement *tam*; by *vyatyayo bahulam* *śap* is the stem-suffix, with Vedic doubling and *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* in the reduplicative; because of *śap*, the guṇa of the light penultimate. Or, by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the stem-suffix is *ślu*, then by *vyatyaya* *śap*; though the root is doubled and so *abhyasta*, by the saying *bahulaṃ chandasīti vaktavyam* the prohibition of guṇa by *nābhyastasyāci piti sārvadhātuke* (Pā. 7-3-87 [?]) does not apply; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*.
*yātam* — root *yā prāpaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person dual; the *tiṅ*-*nighāta*. ‖ 11 ‖

> अस्मे बलानि मघवत्सु धत्तं कृणुतं नो अध्वरं श्रुष्टिमन्तम् ॥ १२ ॥

*(Running head: left "506", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 14 Sū. 93".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 93.12)**

> अग्नीषोमा । पिपृतम् । अर्वतः । नः । आ । प्यायन्ताम् । उस्रियाः । हव्यऽसूदः ।
> अस्मे इति । बलानि । मघवत्ऽसु । धत्तम् । कृणुतम् । नः । अध्वरम् । श्रुष्टिऽमन्तम् ॥ १२ ॥

*agnīṣomā | pipṛtam | arvataḥ | naḥ | ā | pyāyantām | usriyāḥ | havya-sūdaḥ | asme iti | balāni | maghavat-su | dhattam | kṛṇutam | naḥ | adhvaram | śruṣṭi-mantam ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 93.12)**

> हे अग्नीषोमौ नोऽस्माकमर्वतोऽश्वान्पिपृतं । पालयतं । हव्यसूदः क्षीरादिहविष उत्पादयित्र्य उस्रियोऽस्मदीया गावश्चा प्यायन्तां । आस्याय्याताः प्रवृद्धाः सन्तु । मघवत्सु हविर्लक्षणधनयुक्तेष्वस्मे अस्मासु बलानि धत्तं । स्थापयतं । तथा नोऽस्माकमध्वरं यागं श्रुष्टिमन्तं धनयुक्तं कृणुतं । कुरुतं ॥ पिपृतं । पॄ पालनपूरणयोः । पॄ इत्येके । जुहोत्यादित्वाच्छपः श्लुः । ऋर्चिपिपर्त्योश्च इत्यभ्यासस्येत्वं । हव्यसूदः । हव्यं सूदन्ते क्षरन्तीति हव्यसूदः । षूद क्षरणे । क्विप् च । अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्याः शे आदेशः । श्रुष्टिमन्तं । श्रुष्टीति धननाम । शु आश्वश्नुते व्याप्नुते इति श्रुष्टिः । पृषोदरादीनि । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुबिति मतुप उदात्तत्वं ॥

*he agnīṣomau no 'smākam arvato 'śvān pipṛtaṃ | pālayataṃ | havyasūdaḥ kṣīrādihaviṣa utpādayitryā usriyo 'smadīyā gāvaś cā pyāyantāṃ | āpyāyitāḥ pravṛddhāḥ santu | maghavatsu havirlakṣaṇadhanayukteṣv asme asmāsu balāni dhattaṃ | sthāpayataṃ | tathā no 'smākam adhvaraṃ yāgaṃ śruṣṭimantaṃ dhanayuktaṃ kṛṇutaṃ | kurutaṃ ‖ pipṛtaṃ | pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | pṝ ity eke | juhotyāditvāc chapaḥ śluḥ | ṛrcipiparty­oś ca ity abhyāsasyetvaṃ | havyasūdaḥ | havyaṃ sūdante kṣarantīti havyasūdaḥ | ṣūda kṣaraṇe | kvip ca | asme | supāṃ sulug iti saptamyāḥ śe ādeśaḥ | śruṣṭimantaṃ | śruṣṭīti dhananāma | śu āśvaśnute vyāpnute iti śruṣṭiḥ | pṛṣodarādīni | hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matub iti matupa udāttatvaṃ ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni and Soma, *pipṛtam*, protect, cherish, *arvataḥ*, our horses; and let *usriyāḥ*, our cows, which are *havyasūdaḥ* — producers of the milk and other oblations — *ā pyāyantām*, grow full and flourishing. In us, *maghavatsu*, who are rich in wealth in the form of oblations, *balāni dhattam*, place strengths. And make *adhvaram*, our sacrifice, *śruṣṭimantam*, wealth-bearing."

*Grammar tail:* *pipṛtam* — root *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*; *ślu* for *śap* in the *juhotyādi* class; *i* in the reduplicative. *havyasūdaḥ* — "they pour out (*sūdante*) *havya*"; root *ṣūda kṣaraṇe*; *kvip*. *asme* — *śe* for the locative by *supāṃ sulug*. *śruṣṭimantam* — *śruṣṭi* is a name for wealth ("that which pervades quickly"), irregular as in the *pṛṣodarādi* group; the *matup* takes the acute.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 93.12)** *(Kannada)*

*agnīṣomā* — O Agni and Soma deities; *naḥ* — our; *arvataḥ* — horses; *pipṛtam* — protect; *havyasūdaḥ* — those who supply milk and other things needed for the oblations; *usriyāḥ* — our cows; *ā pyāyantām* — let them grow in health and prosper; *maghavatsu* — those with wealth in the form of oblations; *asme* — in us; *balāni* — strengths; *dhattam* — put in and fill; *naḥ* — our; *adhvaram* — sacrifice; *śruṣṭimantam* — rich in wealth; *kṛṇutam* — make.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 93.12** *(Kannada; begins at the foot of p. 506)*

"O Agni and Soma deities, protect our horses. May our cows, which supply the milk and other things needed for oblations, grow in health and prosper. We, who are rich with wealth in the form of oblations —

*(Bhāvārtha, concluded:)* "— fill us with strengths of many kinds. Make our sacrifice endowed with wealth."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 93.12)*

"Agni and Soma, cherish our horses, and may our cows, affording milk that yields butter for oblations be well nourished ; give to us who are affluent, strength to perform religious rites and make our sacrifice productive of wealth." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 93.12)** *(Kannada)*

***arvataḥ*** — "*aśvaḥ, hayaḥ* and the like being read among the names of the horse (Ni. 1-[?] [?]), *arvā* means 'horse'. *arvā* from *ṛ gatau* [*arṣi gacchatīti*], or from *arvatiḥ* [as read, doubtful [?]] (Ni. 11-[?] [?]); because it moves quickly, it is called *arvā*. *arvataḥ* means 'our horses'."

***pipṛtam*** — *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ* | "Here the root *pṝ* in the sense of protecting is used: 'protect our horses'."

***usriyāḥ*** — "*aghnyā, usrā, usriyā* and the like are read among the names of the cow (Ni. 2-[?] [?]). The name *usriyā* is given because it gives *ūṣa* — [as in] *sukhasādhanaṃ kṣīraṃ* — the milk that is a means of happiness; the author of the Nirukta (Ni. 4-[?]) explains it with the example '*pāyase usriyāyāḥ*' (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?], as read, doubtful)."

***śruṣṭimantam*** — "'Wealth-possessing': Sāyaṇa. Skandasvāmin: '*āśiramitemapi sukhanāma etad draṣṭavyam | phalabhūtena sukhena sukhavantam*' [as read, clotted [?]] — that is, even though it is not read among the names of happiness, *śruṣṭi* means happiness; 'endowed with happiness in the form of fruit'; and he goes further: or *śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma | kṣipravantam* — *śruṣṭi* is a name for 'quick': that is, 'bearing fruit swiftly': make our sacrifice swift in yielding fruit."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 93.12)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*pipṛtam* — root *pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ* (some take it as *pṛ*, with a short vowel); in the *juhotyādi* *loṭ*, second person dual, the replacement *tam*; by *ślau* the root is doubled; by *ṛrcipiparty­oś ca* (Pā. 7-4-77 [?]) the *i* in the reduplicative; because *śap* [*ślu*] is *apit*, no guṇa of the root's *ṛ* [the print: since *jit* and doubled]. Since the vocative *agnīṣomā* stands before, by *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* —

### Page 508 (PDF 523)

*(Running head: left "508", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 14 Sū. 93".)*

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 93.12, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly):*

[*pipṛtam*, continued —] "…it counts as non-existent, and since the sentence-initial verb is not preceded by a word, the *nighāta* does not occur; by the suffix accent the final-acute."
*arvataḥ* — the word *arvan*; the accusative plural following, by *arvaṇas trasāvanañaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-127 [?]) *tṛ* is the final replacement.
*havyasūdaḥ* — "*havyaṃ sūdante kṣarantīti havyasūdaḥ*"; root *ṣūda kṣaraṇe*; *kvip*; by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* the *kṛdanta* final member keeps its natural accent, since the first member is a *kāraka*; the accusative plural [read: nominative plural].
*asme* — the word *asmad*; to the locative ending, by *supāṃ sulug*, the replacement *śe*; by *śeṣe lopaḥ* the part up to *m* is elided.
*śruṣṭimantam* — *śruṣṭi* is a name for wealth: "*śu* + *āśu*: that which pervades quickly (*aśnute*) is *śruṣṭiḥ*", an irregular formation in the *pṛṣodarādi* group; "*śruṣṭir asya asti*": by *tad asyāstyasminn iti* the suffix *matup*; by *hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup* (Pā. 6-1-176 [?]) the *matup* takes the acute; the accusative singular.
*kṛṇutam* — root *kṛñ hiṃsāyām*, of the *svādi* class; *loṭ*, second person dual, the replacement *tam*; by *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (Pā. 3-1-73 [?]) the stem-suffix *śnu*; since it is *apit* and *jit* [as read], no guṇa; since it stands at the head of the pāda, no *nighāta*; the final-acute by the suffix accent. Since roots have many meanings, here only the sense 'to do' is accepted; or, with *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, in the *loṭ*, by *vyatyayo bahulam* *śnu* replaces the *u* stem-suffix: hence the desired form. ‖ 12 ‖

**ತೊಂಭತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — Sūkta 94** *(Kannada heading: "the ninety-fourth Sūkta")*

**॥ पञ्चदशेऽनुवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि ॥ — Sāyaṇa's introduction (Sanskrit, printed on p. 509)**

> पञ्चदशेऽनुवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि । तत्रेमं स्तोममिति षोडशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं । आङ्गिरसस्य कुत्सस्यार्षं । पञ्चदशीषोडश्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टा जगत्यः । अग्निर्देवता । पूर्वोर्धे देवा भवतु सुन्वतो रथ इति त्रयः पादा देवदेवत्याः । तन्नो मित्रो वरुण इत्यर्धर्चो लिङ्गोक्तमित्रावरुणादिपदद्वेवत्यः । अथवा तस्यास्यैवाग्नेरेव देवता मित्रावरुणादयस्तु निपातभाक्त्वेनाप्रधानाः । एतत्सर्वमनुक्रान्तं । इमं षोळश कुत्स आग्नेयं तद्द्विस्त्रिष्टुब्बन्तं पूर्वो देवास्त्रयः पादा द्वैवास्तन्नो मित्रोऽर्धर्चो लिङ्गोक्तदेवतो यद्वेवत्यं वा सूक्तमिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकस्याग्नेये क्रतौ जागते छन्दस्येतत्सूक्तं । आश्विनशस्त्रे च । तथा च सूत्रितं । इमं स्तोममर्हते सं जाग्रवद्भिः । आ. ४-१३ [?] । इति ॥ अभिप्लविके षळहेऽन्यस्मिन्नग्निमारुतेऽहन्येतत्सूक्तं जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानं । सूत्रितं च । प्रयज्यव इमं स्तोममित्यग्निमारुतं । आ. ८-८ [?] । इति ॥ तृतीयसवनेऽग्नीधः प्रस्थितयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । इमं स्तोममर्हते जातवेदस इति तार्तीयसवनिक्यः । आ. ५-३ [?] । इति ॥

*pañcadaśe 'nuvāke dvādaśa sūktāni | tatremaṃ stomam iti ṣoḍaśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ | āṅgirasasya kutsasyārṣaṃ | pañcadaśīṣoḍaśyau triṣṭubhau śiṣṭā jagatyaḥ | agnir devatā | pūrvordhe devā bhavatu sunvato ratha iti trayaḥ pādā devadevatyāḥ | tan no mitro varuṇa ity ardharco liṅgoktamitrāvaruṇādipadadvevatyaḥ | athavā tasyāsyaivāgner eva devatā mitrāvaruṇādayas tu nipātabhāktvenāpradhānāḥ | etat sarvam anukrāntaṃ | imaṃ ṣoḷaśa kutsa āgneyaṃ tad dvis triṣṭubbantaṃ pūrvo devās trayaḥ pādā dvaivās tan no mitro 'rdharco liṅgokta­devato yad vevatyaṃ vā sūktam iti ‖ prātaranuvākasyāgneye kratau jāgate chandasy etat sūktaṃ | āśvinaśastre ca | tathā ca sūtritaṃ | imaṃ stomam arhate saṃ jāgravadbhiḥ | Ā. 4-13 [?] | iti ‖ abhiplavike ṣaḷahe 'nyasminn agnimārute 'hany etat sūktaṃ jātavedasy anividdhānaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | prayajyava imaṃ stomam ity agnimārutaṃ | Ā. 8-8 [?] | iti ‖ tṛtīyasavane 'gnīdhaḥ prasthitayājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedasa iti tārtīyasavanikyaḥ | Ā. 5-3 [?] | iti ‖*

*Translation (the printed text is garbled in the Anukramaṇī portion; given as read [?]):* "In the fifteenth anuvāka there are twelve sūktas. Of these the first, *imaṃ stomam*, has sixteen Ṛks; the vision of Kutsa Āṅgirasa. The fifteenth and sixteenth are Triṣṭubh, the rest Jagatī. The deity is Agni. In the first half [of Ṛk 7?], the three pādas *devā bhavatu sunvato rathaḥ* are addressed to the gods; the half-Ṛk *tan no mitro varuṇaḥ* is addressed to the deities named by the words Mitra, Varuṇa and the rest. Or: the deity of the whole is Agni alone, and Mitra, Varuṇa and the others are subordinate, taking a share by mention only. All this is recorded in the Anukramaṇī: '*imaṃ ṣoḷaśa kutsa āgneyaṃ…*'. This sūkta is applied in the Āgneya *kratu* of the *prātaranuvāka*, in the Jagatī metre, and in the *Āśvina-śastra*; so it is prescribed: '*imaṃ stomam arhate saṃ jāgravadbhiḥ*' (Ā. 4-13 [?]). It is also applied, as a *jātavedasya* *nividdhāna*, on the other Agni-Māruta day of the *abhiplava ṣaḷaha*; prescribed: '*prayajyava imaṃ stomam ity agnimārutam*' (Ā. 8-8 [?]). At the third pressing it is the *prasthitayājyā* of the Agnīdh; prescribed: '*imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedasa iti tārtīyasavanikyaḥ*' (Ā. 5-3 [?])."

**अनुवादवु — Anuvāda (Kannada)**

"With this sūkta the fifteenth anuvāka of the First Maṇḍala begins. In this anuvāka there are twelve sūktas (94–105 [?]). Of these, the first sūkta, beginning *imaṃ stomam*, has sixteen Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa, son of Aṅgiras; the deity is Agni. The fifteenth and sixteenth Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: '*imaṃ ṣoḷaśa kutsa āgneyaṃ tad dvis triṣṭubbantaṃ pūrvo devās trayaḥ pādā dvaivās tan no mitro 'rdharco liṅgoktadevato yad vevatyaṃ vā sūktam iti*' [as printed, garbled [?]]. In the eighth Ṛk of this sūkta the first three pādas are addressed to the gods and the last pāda to Agni. For the second half of the sixteenth Ṛk the six deities Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Pṛthivī and Dyaus are named; or it may be said that Agni is the principal deity. Varuṇa and the others are not principal. It is shown by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra '*imaṃ stomam arhate saṃ jāgravadbhiḥ*' (Ā. 4-13 [?]), that this sūkta is applied in reciting the Jagatī mantras belonging to the Āgneya *kratu* in reciting the *prātaranuvāka* mantras, and for the mantras of the *Āśvina-śastra*; and, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains by the sūtra '*prayajyava imaṃ stomam ity agnimārutam*' (Ā. 8-8 [?]), on the sixth day of the *abhiplava* sacrifice this sūkta is to be used, as a *nivid*-containing hymn connected with Jātaveda, for the Agni-Māruta *śastra* mantras. At the third pressing the Ṛtvij called Āgnīdhra is to use the first Ṛk of this sūkta, *imaṃ stomam*, as the *prasthitayājyā* mantra" *(continued on p. 510)*

*imam | stomam | arhate | jāta-vedase | ratham-iva | sam | mahema | manīṣayā | bhadrā | hi | naḥ | pra-matiḥ | asya | saṃ-sadi | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.1)**

> अर्हते पूज्याय जातवेदसे जातानामुत्पन्नानां वेदित्रे जातप्रज्ञाय जातधनाय वाग्नयेः [read: *agnaye*] मनीषया निशितया बुद्ध्येमममेतत्सूक्तरूपं स्तोमं स्तोत्रं रथमिव यथा तक्षा रथं संस्करोति तथा सं महेम । सम्यक् पूजितं कुर्मः । अस्माग्नेः संसदि संभजने सोऽस्माकं प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टा बुद्धिर्भद्रा हि कल्याणी समर्था खलु । अतस्तया बुद्ध्या स्तुमं इत्यर्थः । हे अग्ने तव सख्ये ऽस्माकं त्वया सह सखित्वे सति वयं मा रिषाम । हिंसिता न भवाम । अस्मान्रक्षेत्यर्थः ॥ अर्हते । अर्ह पूजायां । अर्हः प्रशंसायां । पा. ३-२-१३३ [?] । इति लटः शत्रादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे शतुश्चादुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । महेमा । मह पूजायां । रिषाम । रिष हिंसायां । व्यत्ययेन शः । तव । युष्मदस्मदोर्ङसीत्यादिनाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

*arhate pūjyāya jātavedase jātānām utpannānāṃ veditre jātaprajñāya jātadhanāya vāgnaye manīṣayā niśitayā buddhyemam etat sūktarūpaṃ stomaṃ stotraṃ ratham iva yathā takṣā rathaṃ saṃskaroti tathā saṃ mahema | samyak pūjitaṃ kurmaḥ | asmād agneḥ saṃsadi saṃbhajane so 'smākaṃ pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭā buddhir bhadrā hi kalyāṇī samarthā khalu | atas tayā buddhyā stumaṃ ity arthaḥ | he agne tava sakhye 'smākaṃ tvayā saha sakhitve sati vayaṃ mā riṣāma | hiṃsitā na bhavāma | asmān rakṣety arthaḥ ‖ arhate | arha pūjāyāṃ | arhaḥ praśaṃsāyāṃ | Pā. 3-2-133 [?] iti laṭaḥ śatrādeśaḥ | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatve śatuś cādupadeśāl lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | mahemā | maha pūjāyāṃ | riṣāma | riṣa hiṃsāyāṃ | vyatyayena śaḥ | tava | yuṣmadasmador ṅasīty ādinādyudāttatvaṃ ‖*

*Translation:* "To Agni, *arhate*, the worthy, *jātavedase*, the knower of all that is born, or one of born wisdom, or of born wealth: *manīṣayā*, with a sharpened understanding, *imam stomam*, this praise in the form of a sūkta, *ratham iva*, as the carpenter fashions a chariot, so *saṃ mahema* — we make it well-honoured, we fashion it. In Agni's *saṃsadi*, in the assembly [or: in the company, the worship] of Agni, *asya naḥ pramatiḥ*, that excellent understanding of ours is *bhadrā*, auspicious, capable. Therefore with that understanding we praise: this is the meaning. O Agni, *tava sakhye*, in your friendship — we being in friendship with you — *vayam mā riṣāma*, may we not be harmed. Protect us."

*Grammar tail:* *arhate* — root *arha pūjāyām*, with the sense of praise; *śatṛ* for the *laṭ* (Pā. 3-2-133 [?]); the root's accent remains. *mahemā* — root *maha pūjāyām*. *riṣāma* — root *riṣa hiṃsāyām*; *śa* by *vyatyaya*. *tava* — the initial acute by *yuṣmadasmador ṅasi…*.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 94.1)** *(Kannada)*

*arhate* — to the worthy of worship; *jātavedase* — to Agni, who knows all that has been born, or who has wealth, or who has wisdom; *manīṣayā* — with our (keen) understanding; *imaṃ stomam* — this praise in the form of a sūkta; *rathamiva* — as a chariot-maker builds a chariot; *saṃ mahema* — we build with great skill; *asya* — of this Agni; *saṃsadi* — in the assembly of worship; *naḥ* — our; *pramatiḥ* — excellent understanding; *bhadrā hi* — is auspicious indeed; *agne* — O Agni; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — in friendship (for the sake of); *vayam* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not be injured (favour us).

### Page 512 (PDF 527)

*(Running head: left "512", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 15 Sū. 94".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 94.1** *(Kannada)*

"To Agni, who is worthy of worship and possesses knowledge that knows everything: as a chariot-maker fashions a chariot for a king, so we too, with our keen understanding, skilfully fashion this praise in the form of a sūkta. In the worship of this divine Agni our understanding is auspicious. O Agni, because of friendship with you, favour us so that we are not harmed by enemies."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 94.1)*

"To him who is worthy of praise, and all-knowing, we construct, with our minds, this hymn, as (a workman makes) a car; happy is our understanding when engaged in his adoration ; O Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 94.1)** *(Kannada)*

***jātavedase*** — *jātāni veda; jātāni vainaṃ viduḥ; jāte jāte vidyate iti vā; jātavitto vā jātadhanaḥ; jātavidyo vā jātaprajñaḥ* (Ni. 7-19 [?]) | "The author of the Nirukta explains it thus: [Agni is] 'one who knows all that is born'; or 'all that is born knows him'; or 'he is present in everything born'; or 'one who has wealth that is born'; or 'one whose wisdom is born': that is, he who knows all that has arisen; or all that has arisen knows him; or he abides in all that has arisen; or he has all the wealth that has arisen; or he has knowledge of everything. In the *Bṛhaddevatā* too he explains in detail the nature and the places of Jātavedas:"

> इहाग्निर्भूतैस्त्र्वृषिभिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळितः ।
> जातवेदास्तु तोमध्ये स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि ॥

*ihāgnir bhūtais tr ṛṣibhir loke stutibhir īḷitaḥ | jātavedās tu to madhye stuto vaiśvānaro divi ‖*  (Bṛ. De. 1-[?] [?]; the text of the second pāda is garbled in the print and read as given [?])

*Gloss, mine and tentative:* "Here in the world Agni is praised by the seers with hymns; in the middle region Jātavedas; in heaven Vaiśvānara."

"— in this verse the ṛṣis are said to praise the Agni who is on the earth as Agni, the one in the mid-region as Jātavedas, and the one in the heavenly world as Vaiśvānara; and he continues the same idea:"

> वैश्वानरं श्रितो ह्यग्निरग्निं वैश्वानरः श्रितः ।
> अनयोर्जातवेदास्तु तथ्यैते जातवेदसी ॥

*vaiśvānaraṃ śrito hy agnir agniṃ vaiśvānaraḥ śritaḥ | anayor jātavedās tu tathyaite jātavedasī ‖*  (Bṛ. De. 1-[?] [?]; read as printed, doubtful [?])

"— Agni abides in Vaiśvānara and Vaiśvānara in Agni; Jātavedas is in both of these; and he explains both as the two portions of Jātavedas. Thus, having first told the places of Jātavedas in the first chapter, in the second chapter he gives the explanation of his nature:"

> भूतानि वेद यज्ञातो जातवेदाथ कथ्यते ।

*bhūtāni veda yaj jāto jātavedātha kathyate |*  (Bṛ. De. [?] [?]; read as printed, continued on p. 513)

> यच्चैष जातविद्योऽभूद्वित्तं जातोऽधिवेति वा ॥

*yac caiṣa jātavidyo 'bhūd vittaṃ jāto 'dhiveti vā ‖*  (Bṛ. De. [?] [?]; as printed)

> विद्यते सर्वभूतैर्हि यद्वा जातः पुनः पुनः ।
> तेनैष मध्यभागेन्द्रो जातवेदा इति स्तुतः ॥

*vidyate sarvabhūtair hi yad vā jātaḥ punaḥ punaḥ | tenaiṣa madhyabhāgendro jātavedā iti stutaḥ ‖*  (Bṛ. De. [?] [?]; as printed)

*Gloss, mine and tentative:* "…and because he has become knowing of all that is born, or has wealth, or is known [or found] among the born; or because he is known by all beings, or is born again and again — therefore he, the Indra of the middle region, is praised as Jātavedas."

"— in the *Bṛhaddevatā* it is explained that Agni is praised as Jātavedas, like Indra, being a dweller in the middle world: because he knows everything the moment it comes into being, or because knowledge arises in him, or because, the moment he is born, he obtains all wealth, or because he is known by all beings again and again, being born anew each time. *Jātavedase* means: to Agni of such nature."

***imaṃ stomaṃ ratham iva saṃ mahema*** — *yathā takṣā rathaṃ saṃskaroti tathā samyak pūjitaṃ kurmaḥ* | "As a chariot-maker, for the delight of the king, makes a chariot in a way that gives delight to those travelling in it, so we too, with finely wrought speech, a speech that is pleasant to hear, and with a feeling of faith, fashion in a fitting manner these hymns, which bring delight to you, for offering to you: this is the meaning. In many contexts the poetic composition of a hymn is compared to the building of a chariot, to show how much skill is the chief thing in the making of the hymn. Here are some examples —"

> अस्मा इदु स्तोमं सं हिनोमि रथं न तष्टेव तत्सिनाय ।

*asmā id u stomaṃ saṃ hinomi rathaṃ na taṣṭeva tatsināya |*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-4 [?]; numerals as read, doubtful)

> वस्त्रेव भद्रा सुकृता वसूयू रथं न धीरः स्वपा अतक्षम् ।

*vastreva bhadrā sukṛtā vasūyū rathaṃ na dhīraḥ svapā atakṣam |*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?] [?])

> एवेन्द्राय वृषभाय वृष्णे ब्रह्माकर्म भृगवो न रथम् ।

*evendrāya vṛṣabhāya vṛṣṇe brahmākarma bhṛgavo na ratham |*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-20 [?])

> एतं वां स्तोममश्विनावकर्मातक्षाम भृगवो न रथम् ।

*etaṃ vāṃ stomam aśvināv akarmātakṣāma bhṛgavo na ratham |*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-14 [?])

*Gloss, mine and tentative (for the group):* "For him I fashion this hymn, as a carpenter [fashions] a chariot for the hirer. — Like a fair, well-made garment, I, the wise one, skilful, fashioned [the hymn] as a chariot. — So for Indra the bull, the showerer, we have made the prayer, as the Bhṛgus [made] a chariot. — This hymn for you, O Aśvins, we have made, we have fashioned it, as the Bhṛgus a chariot."

"— in such Ṛks, the skill in fashioning a hymn of poetic form and the skill in fashioning a chariot are shown as alike, and the greatness of hymns is praised."

***tava sakhye vayaṃ mā riṣāma*** — "If, having made friendship with Agni, one performs sacrifice with faith, directed to him, then because Agni's help is assured, no enemy can harm him, nor can any harm of another sort occur."

*na tasya māyayā cana ripur īśīta martyaḥ | yo agnaye dadāśa havyadātibhiḥ ‖*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?] [?]; numerals as read, doubtful)

*mā te sakhāyaḥ sadam id riṣāma yacchā tokāya tanayāya śaṃ yoḥ |*  (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?] [?]; numerals as read, doubtful)

"— in such Ṛks, in prayers at all times, the idea is seen that no harm can come to the sacrificer who has obtained Agni's friendship. In this sūkta, down to its end, this same order, like a refrain, is read in each Ṛk as its fourth pāda."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 94.1)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*arhate* — root *arha pūjāyām*; by *arhaḥ praśaṃsāyām* (Pā. 3-2-133 [?]), since the sense of praise is chiefly intended, the *śatṛ* for the *laṭ*; *śap* as stem-suffix; the word *arhat*; since *śap* is *pit* it is unaccented; since the *lasārvadhātuka* (*śatṛ*) follows an *udāttopadeśa* root, by *tāsyanudāttetṅ…* (Pā. 6-1-186 [?]) it is unaccented; the accent of the root remains; the dative singular.
*mahema* — root *maha pūjāyām*; *vidhiliṅ*, first person plural, *mas*; by *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* the elision of the *s*; the augment *yāsuṭ*; the stem-suffix *śap*; by *ato yeyaḥ* the replacement *iyā*; the elision of *y*; the *nighāta* following a word.
*sakhye* — "*sakhyur bhāvaḥ sakhyam*"; by *sakhyur yaḥ* (Pā. 5-1-126 [?]) the suffix *ya*; the final-acute by the suffix accent; the locative singular.
*riṣāma* — root *riṣa hiṃsāyām*; *liṅ* [read: *āśīrliṅ*/*luṅ*, as printed *loṭ* first person]; *mas*; by *vyatyayo bahulam* the stem-suffix *śa*; by *āḍuttamasya pic ca* (Pā. 3-4-92 [?]) the augment *āṭ*; since it follows a word [*mā*], the *nighāta*; by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* the lengthening in the Saṃhitā.
*tava* — the word *yuṣmad*; the genitive singular; by *tevamāvekavacane* [as read, *tava mamau ṅasi*] the replacement *tava*; for the *ṅas* ending, *a* [as printed]; the elision of the *s*-ending part; by *yuṣmadasmador ṅasi* (Pā. 6-1-211 [?]) the initial-acute. ‖ 1 ‖

*(printer's ornament)*

### Page 515 (PDF 530)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 30 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 515.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.2)** *(Jagatī)*

> यस्मै त्वमायजसे स साधत्यनर्वा क्षेति दधते सुवीर्यम् ।
> स तूताव नैनमश्नोत्यंहतिरग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ २ ॥

*yasmai tvam āyajase sa sādhaty anarvā kṣeti dadhate suvīryam | sa tūtāva nainam aśnoty aṃhatir agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.2)**

> यस्मै । त्वम् । आऽयजसे । सः । साधति । अनर्वा । क्षेति । दधते । सुऽवीर्यम् ।
> सः । तूताव । न । एनम् । अश्नोति । अंहतिः । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ २ ॥

*yasmai | tvam | ā-yajase | saḥ | sādhati | anarvā | kṣeti | dadhate | su-vīryam | saḥ | tūtāva | na | enam | aśnoti | aṃhatiḥ | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.2)**

> यस्मै यजमानाय हे अग्ने त्वमायजसे देवानामभिमुख्येन यजसि स यजमानः साधति । स्वाभिलषितं साधयति । प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । किंच स यजमानोऽनर्वा शत्रुभिरप्रत्यृतः सन् क्षेति । निवसति । तथा सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्योपेतं धनं दधते । धारयति । प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । धृत्वा च स यजमानस्तूताव । वर्धते । एनं यजमानमंहतिर्दारिद्र्यं नाश्नोति । न प्राप्नोति । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ साधति । षिधु संराद्धौ । चिञि सिद्ध्यतेरपारलौकिके । पा. ६-१-४९ [?] । इत्यात्वं । छन्दस्युभयथेति शपस आर्धधातुकत्वाण्णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । क्षेति । क्षि निवासगत्योः । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । दधते । दध धारणे । भौवादिकः । तूताव । तु इति वृद्ध्यर्थः सौत्रो धातुः । अस्माच्छन्दसो लिट् । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वं । अश्नोति । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । अंहतिः । हन्तेरंह च । उ. ४-६३ [?] । इत्यतिप्रत्ययः । चिदित्यनुवृत्तेरन्तोदात्तत्वं ॥

*yasmai yajamānāya he agne tvam āyajase devānām abhimukhyena yajasi sa yajamānaḥ sādhati | svābhilaṣitaṃ sādhayati | prāpnotīty arthaḥ | kiṃca sa yajamāno 'narvā śatrubhir apratyṛtaḥ san kṣeti | nivasati | tathā suvīryaṃ śobhanavīryopetaṃ dhanaṃ dadhate | dhārayati | prāpnotīty arthaḥ | dhṛtvā ca sa yajamānas tūtāva | vardhate | enaṃ yajamānam aṃhatir dāridryaṃ nāśnoti | na prāpnoti | anyat pūrvavat ‖ sādhati | ṣidhu saṃrāddhau | ciñi siddhyater apāralaukike | Pā. 6-1-49 [?] ity ātvaṃ | chandasy ubhayatheti śapasa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | kṣeti | kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | dadhate | dadha dhāraṇe | bhauvādikaḥ | tūtāva | tu iti vṛddhyarthaḥ sautro dhātuḥ | asmāc chandaso liṭ | tujāditvād abhyasasya dīrghatvaṃ | aśnoti | vyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ | aṃhatiḥ | hanter aṃha ca | U. 4-63 [?] ity atipratyayaḥ | cid ity anuvṛtter antodāttatvaṃ ‖*

*Translation:* "The sacrificer for whom, O Agni, you *āyajase*, sacrifice facing the gods, *sādhati* — he accomplishes his desires, obtains them. Further, that sacrificer, *anarvā*, unassailed by enemies, *kṣeti* — dwells; and *dadhate*, holds, obtains, *suvīryam*, wealth that has excellent strength; and having obtained it he *tūtāva*, thrives. *Aṃhatiḥ*, poverty, does not *aśnoti*, reach, this sacrificer. The rest as before."

*Grammar tail:* *sādhati* — root *ṣidhu saṃrāddhau*; the *ā*-substitution (Pā. 6-1-49 [?]); *ṇilopa* since the stem-suffix is *ārdhadhātuka* by *chandasy ubhayathā*. *kṣeti* — root *kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*; *luk* of the stem-suffix. *dadhate* — root *dadha dhāraṇe*, *bhvādi*. *tūtāva* — *tu*, a *sautra* root in the sense of growth; *liṭ* in Chandas; the reduplicative lengthened as in the *tujādi* group. *aśnoti* — *parasmaipada* by *vyatyaya*. *aṃhatiḥ* — *aṃha* is the replacement for *han*; the suffix *ati* (U. 4-63 [?]); final-acute by *cit*.

### Page 516 (PDF 531)

*(Running head: left "516", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 15 Sū. 94".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 94.2)** *(Kannada)*

*agne* — O Agni; *tvam* — you; *yasmai* — for which sacrificer; *āyajase* — you perform sacrifice (with reference to the deities); *saḥ* — that sacrificer; *sādhati* — obtains his desired ends; *anarvā* — free from the fear of enemies' attack, avoiding subjection to enemies; *kṣeti* — lives carefree; *suvīryam* — wealth that is a means to excellent strength; *dadhate* — obtains; (thereafter) *saḥ* — that sacrificer; *tūtāva* — obtains prosperity; *enam* — this sacrificer; *aṃhatiḥ* — poverty; *na aśnoti* — does not reach; *agne* — O Agni; *tava sakhye* — through friendship with you; *vayam* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not be harmed (favour us).

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 94.2** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni, the sacrificer for whom you perform sacrifices with reference to the deities obtains his desired ends. Free from the fear of enemies' attack, he lives without care. He obtains wealth that is a means to excellent strength, and obtains prosperity. Poverty never touches him. O Agni, through friendship with you, favour us and protect us so that we are not harmed."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 94.2)*

"He for whom you sacrifice, accomplishes (his objects), abides free from aggression, and enjoys (wealth, the source of) strength ; he prospers and poverty never approaches him ; let us not suffer injury, through your friendship." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 94.2)** *(Kannada)*

***tvaṃ yasmai āyajase sa sādhati*** — "'The sacrificer for whom you, performing sacrifice with reference to the deities, act, obtains his desired ends': this is the meaning. Agni, as soon as he is born, creates the sacrifice and performs sacrifice for men with reference to the deities. Accepting the prayer of the householder, according to his need he is the *purohita*, the *ṛtvij*, the *hotṛ* and the *brahman*, and, offering oblations to the deities, causes their favour to be obtained for the sacrificer in his house. In about two hundred contexts in Ṛks that praise Agni, such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1 [?]; 1-13-1 [?]; 1-31-1 [?]; 1-[?]-2 [?] and so on, Agni is described as the principal in the sacrifices. Because he is himself the sacrifice-soul, and because he is the full cause of the satisfaction of the deities, the idea is that the favour of the deities of every kind can be achieved through him."

***anarvā*** — *anarvā apratyṛtaḥ* [*apratyṛto 'nyasmin*] (Ni. 6-[?] [?]) | "This word is used in many contexts in the sense 'one who has no other refuge or subjection'. In Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-40-6 [?]; 4-[?]-10 [?]; 5-[?]-3 [?]; 6-20-[?] [?]; 10-[?]-3 [?] it gives the sense that the deities, unopposed by enemies and not subject to them, show their prowess. So here too: the sacrificer who has obtained Agni's favour lives independently, neither conquered by enemies nor subject to them."

***kṣeti*** — "Living independently, dwelling at his own dwelling-places, he lives in happiness: this is the idea."

***tūtāva*** — "From the root *tu*, which gives the sense of 'growth' or 'strength', *tūtāva*. 'He has obtained growth' or 'he has obtained strength': this is the idea."

***aṃhatiḥ*** — *aṃhatiś cāṃhaś cāṃhuś ca hanteḥ* (Ni. 4-[?]) | "From the root *han* the word *aṃhati* is formed. It means 'to injure, to afflict'. Here it is affliction in the form of poverty. The meaning is that for the sacrificer who has Agni's favour, *aṃhatiḥ nāśnoti* — poverty does not touch him."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 94.2)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*yajase* — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; *laṭ*, second person singular; since *yasmai* is connected, the *nighāta* does not occur; since the suffix follows an *udāttopadeśa* root it is unaccented; then the accent of the root remains.
*sādhati* — root *ṣidhu saṃrāddhau*; since the sense of the instigator is shown, by *hetumati ca* the suffix *ṇic*; by *ciñi siddhyater aparalaukike* (Pā. 6-1-49 [?]) the *ā* [for the root's *i*]; by *chandasy ubhayathā*, as the stem-suffix is *ārdhadhātuka*, the elision of *ṇi* by *ṇer aniṭi*; the *nighāta* following a word.
*kṣeti* — root *kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*, *bhvādi*; *liṭ* [as printed; the form is the *laṭ*] third person singular, *tip*; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the *luk* of the stem-suffix (*śap*); because of the suffix the guṇa of the root's *i*; the *nighāta* following a word.
*dadhate* — root *dadha dhāraṇe*, *bhvādi*, with an *ātmanepada* because it is *anudāttet*; *laṭ*, third person singular; since a finite verb stands after a word, the *nighāta* does not occur; since *śap* is *pit* it is unaccented; since the *lasārvadhātuka* (*te*) follows an *udāttopadeśa* root, by *tāsyanudāttetṅ…* it is unaccented; the accent of the root remains. —

*suvīryam* — in the *bahuvrīhi* the accent of *su* is set aside by *vīravīryau ca* (Pā. 6-2-120 [?]), and the final member takes the initial-acute.
*tūtāva* — *tu* is a *sautra* root, in the sense of growth; in the present sense, by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. 3-4-6 [?]) the *liṭ*; because of it the root is doubled; since *ṇit* follows, by *ata upadhāyāḥ* the vṛddhi of the penultimate; since it belongs to the *tujādi* group, by *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya* (Pā. 6-1-7 [?]) the reduplicative is lengthened; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*.
*aśnoti* — root *aśū vyāptau*; by *vyatyayo bahulam* the *parasmaipada*; *laṭ*, third person singular; the *tiṅ*-*nighāta*.
*aṃhatiḥ* — root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; by *hanter aṃha ca* (U. 4-[?] [?]) the suffix *ati*; because of it the root is replaced by *aṃha*; by *vahiśriyuśvidrū…* [as read, partly clotted [?]] *cit* continues, so by *citaḥ* the final-acute.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.3)**

> हे अग्ने त्वात्वां समिधं सम्यगिद्धं कर्तुं शकेम । शक्ता भूयास्म । त्वं च धियोऽस्मदीयानि दर्शपूर्णमासादीनि कर्माणि साधय । निष्पादय । त्वयि हि सर्वे यागा निष्पाद्यन्ते । यस्मात्त्वे त्वय्यग्नावाहुतं ऋत्विग्भिः प्रक्षिप्तं चरुपुरोडाशादिकं हविर्देवा अदन्ति भक्षयन्ति तस्मात्त्वं साधयेत्यर्थः । अपि च त्वमादित्यानदितेः पुत्रान् सर्वान्देवानावह । अस्मद्यज्ञार्थमानय । तान्द्वीदानीमेव वयमुश्मसि । कामयामहे । अस्त्वन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ शकेम । शक्लृ शक्तौ । लिङ्याशिष्यङ् । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे ऽच एव स्वरः शिष्यते । समिधं । इन्धी दीप्तौ । अस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणः कर्मणि क्विप् । त्वे । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्येकवचनस्य शे आदेशः । उश्मसि । वश कान्तौ । इदन्तो मसिः । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणं ॥

*he agne tvā tvāṃ samidhaṃ samyag iddhaṃ kartuṃ śakema | śaktā bhūyāsma | tvaṃ ca dhiyo 'smadīyāni darśapūrṇamāsādīni karmāṇi sādhaya | niṣpādaya | tvayi hi sarve yāgā niṣpādyante | yasmāt tve tvayy agnāv āhutaṃ ṛtvigbhiḥ prakṣiptaṃ carupuroḍāśādikaṃ havir devā adanti bhakṣayanti tasmāt tvaṃ sādhayety arthaḥ | api ca tvam ādityān aditeḥ putrān sarvān devān āvaha | asmadyajñārtham ānaya | tān dvīdānīm eva vayam uśmasi | kāmayāmahe | astv anyat pūrvavat ‖ śakema | śakḷ śaktau | liṅy āśiṣy aṅ | adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve 'ca eva svaraḥ śiṣyate | samidhaṃ | indhī dīptau | asmāt saṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ karmaṇi kvip | tve | supāṃ sulug iti saptamyekavacanasya śe ādeśaḥ | uśmasi | vaśa kāntau | idanto masiḥ | adādityāc chapo luk | grahijyety ādinā saṃprasāraṇaṃ ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni, may we be able to make you *samidham*, well kindled; may we be capable. And you, *sādhaya*, accomplish *dhiyaḥ*, our rites such as the new- and full-moon. For all sacrifices are accomplished in you. Because *tve*, in you, in Agni, *āhutam*, the oblation cast in by the priests — the *havis* such as *caru* and *puroḍāśa* — the gods *adanti*, eat: therefore accomplish: this is the meaning. Moreover bring *ādityān*, the sons of Aditi, all the gods, for our sacrifice; *tān hi uśmasi*, we desire them, now. The rest as before."

*Grammar tail:* *śakema* — root *śakḷ śaktau*; the *āśīrliṅ*, with *aṅ* [as read]. *samidham* — root *indhī dīptau*; *kvip* in the passive sense. *tve* — *śe* for the locative singular. *uśmasi* — root *vaśa kāntau*; *masi* with *i*; *luk* of *śap* (*adādi*); *saṃprasāraṇa* by *grahijyā…*.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 94.3)** *(Kannada)*

*agne* — O Agni; *tvā* — you; *samidham* — blazing; (to make [you]) *śakema* — may we be able; *dhiyaḥ* — our (new- and full-moon and other) rites; *sādhaya* — accomplish [one after another] (because); *tve* — in you; *āhutam* — offered, cast in; *haviḥ* — oblations (*caru*, *puroḍāśa* etc.); *devāḥ* — the deities; *adanti* — eat; *tvam* — you; *ādityān* — all the deities, sons of Aditi; *ā vaha* — (to the sacrifice) bring and come; *hi* — because; *tān* — them; *uśmasi* — we desire; *agne* — O Agni; *tava* — with you; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayam* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer any harm.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 94.3** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni, give us the power to make you blaze. Because the deities eat the *caru*, *puroḍāśa* and the like offered in you, accomplish our new- and full-moon and other rites. Bring all the deities, the sons of Aditi, whom we love and desire, to our sacrifice. O Agni, through friendship with you, may no harm come to us."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 94.3)*

"May we be able to kindle you ; make the rite perfect, for through you the gods partake of the offered oblations ; bring hither the Aditayas [sic], for we love them ; let us not suffer injury, through your friendship." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 94.3)** *(Kannada)*

***dhiyaḥ*** — "*āpaḥ, āpnaḥ, daṃsaḥ* and the like being read among the names of works (Ni. 2-1 [?]), *dhiyaḥ* means 'works'. In this context, it is the prayer: 'help our new- and full-moon and other rites to be accomplished'."

***uśmasi*** — "*vaṣṭi, uśmasi, veti* and the like being read among the eighteen names of acts of wishing (Ni. 2-6 [?]), the meaning here is 'we long for'."

***ādityān*** — *ādityaḥ kasmād ādatte rasān ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām dīpto bhāseti vādites tu putra iti vā* (Ni. 2-13 [?]) | "'From what is *āditya*? He takes (*ādatte*) the juices; he takes the lustre of the lights; he shines with lustre; or he is the son of Aditi': the author of the Nirukta explains the meaning of the word *āditya* as one who takes up the juices (draws them up), or who takes the radiance of the orbs of light (takes in their splendour), or who shines with his own splendour, or as the son of Aditi. For the Sun the word is a name of Parjanya [as read [?]]. But since the plural *ādityān* occurs in this Ṛk, it is to be understood that the word *āditya* applies not only to the Sun but also to the other deities. The author of the Nirukta himself, explaining this, says: *vayam anyāsām api devatānām ādityaprapādā stutayo bhavanti tad yathaitan mitrasya varuṇasyāryamṇo dakṣasya bhagasyāṃśasyeti* (Ni. 2-13 [?]): 'the praises of the Ādityas, too, are those of other deities': he explains that praises addressed to the Ādityas apply to Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Dakṣa, Bhaga and Aṃśa, and gives examples. In the Ṛksaṃhitā, in the hymns addressed to the Ādityas —

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 94.3)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*śakema* — root *śakḷ śaktau*; *āśīrliṅ*, first person plural, *mas*; by *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* the elision of the *s*; by *liṅyāśiṣy aṅ* (Pā. 3-1-86 [?]) the suffix *aṅ* for the root [as read]; since the root is *adupadeśa* and a *lasārvadhātuka* follows, by *tāsyanudāttetṅ…* the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented; then the accent of the suffix *aṅ* remains, so the middle syllable is acute; since it stands at the head of the pāda, no *nighāta*.
*samidham* — root *iñdhī dīptau*; since it belongs to the *saṃpadādi* group, *kvip* in the passive sense by *saṃpadādibhyaḥ kvip*; by *aniditāṃ…* the elision of the nasal [*n*] of the penultimate; the word ends in *dh*; the accusative singular.
*adanti* — root *ada bhakṣaṇe*; *laṭ*, third person plural; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*.
*ādityān* — by *dīrghād aṭi samānapāde* the *n* becomes *ru*; by *āto 'ṭi nityam* the *ā* is nasalized.
*tve* — the word *yuṣmad*; in the locative singular, the part up to *m* is replaced by *tva*; by *śeṣe lopaḥ* the *ad* is elided; by *supāṃ sulug* the ending is replaced by *śe*.
*uśmasi* — root *vaśa kāntau*; *adādi*, *laṭ*, first person plural, with the suffix *masi*; by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* the *luk* of *śap*; since the suffix is *jit*, by *grahijyāvayi…* (Pā. 6-1-16 [?]) the *saṃprasāraṇa*; the preceding form; by *idanto masiḥ* (Pā. 7-1-46 [?]) —

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.4)** *(Jagatī)*

> भरामेध्मं कृणवामा हवींषि ते चितयन्तः पर्वणापर्वणा वयम् ।
> जीवातवे प्रतरं साधया धियोऽग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ ४ ॥

*bharāmedhmaṃ kṛṇavāmā havīṃṣi te citayantaḥ parvaṇā-parvaṇā vayam | jīvātave prataraṃ sādhayā dhiyo 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.4)**

> भराम । इध्मम् । कृणवाम । हवींषि । ते । चितयन्तः । पर्वणाऽपर्वणा । वयम् ।
> जीवातवे । प्रऽतरम् । साधय । धियः । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ ४ ॥

*bharāma | idhmam | kṛṇavāma | havīṃṣi | te | citayantaḥ | parvaṇā-parvaṇā | vayam | jīvātave | pra-taram | sādhaya | dhiyaḥ | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.4)**

> हे अग्ने त्वद्दाहार्थमिध्ममिन्धनसाधनमेकविंशतिदारात्मकं समित्समूहं भरामः । संपादयामः । तदनन्तरं ते तुभ्यं हवींषि चरुपुरोडाशादीन्यन्नानि वयं कृणवाम । करवाम । किं कुर्वन्तः । पर्वणापर्वणा प्रतिपक्षमावृत्ताभ्यां दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां चिन्तयन्तस्त्वां प्रज्ञापयन्तः । स त्वं जीवातवेऽस्माकं जीवनौषधाय चिरकालावस्थानाय धियः कर्माण्यग्निहोत्रादीनि प्रतरं प्रकृष्टतरं साधय । निष्पादय । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ चितयन्तः । चिती संज्ञाने । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । पर्वणापर्वणा । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति वीप्सायां द्विर्भावः । तस्य परमाम्रेडितमिति परस्याम्रेडितसंज्ञायामनुदात्तं चेत्यनुदात्तत्वं । प्रतरं । तरबन्तात्प्रशब्दात्क्रियाप्रकर्षे वर्तमानादमु च च्छन्दसि । पा. ५-४-१२ [?] । इत्यमुप्रत्ययः ॥

*he agne tvaddāhārtham idhmam indhanasādhanam ekaviṃśatidārātmakaṃ samitsamūhaṃ bharāmaḥ | saṃpādayāmaḥ | tadanantaraṃ te tubhyaṃ havīṃṣi carupuroḍāśādīny annāni vayaṃ kṛṇavāma | karavāma | kiṃ kurvantaḥ | parvaṇā-parvaṇā pratipakṣam āvṛttābhyāṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ cintayantas tvāṃ prajñāpayantaḥ | sa tvaṃ jīvātave 'smākaṃ jīvanauṣadhāya cirakālāvasthānāya dhiyaḥ karmāṇy agnihotrādīni prataraṃ prakṛṣṭataraṃ sādhaya | niṣpādaya | anyat pūrvavat ‖ citayantaḥ | citī saṃjñāne | saṃjñāpūrvakasya vidher anityatvāl laghūpadhaguṇābhāvaḥ | parvaṇā-parvaṇā | nityavīpsayor iti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ | tasya paramāmreḍitam iti parasyāmreḍitasaṃjñāyām anudāttaṃ cety anudāttatvaṃ | prataraṃ | tarabantāt prāśabdāt kriyāprakarṣe vartamānād amu ca chandasi | Pā. 5-4-12 [?] ity amupratyayaḥ ‖*

*Translation:* "O Agni, for your burning *idhmam* — the means of kindling, a bundle of twenty-one logs — *bharāma*, we gather, we prepare. Thereafter *havīṃṣi*, oblations — *caru*, *puroḍāśa* and the foods — *kṛṇavāma*, we make for you. How? *Parvaṇā-parvaṇā* — at each *parvan*, each junction of the lunar fortnight, by the new-moon and the full-moon sacrifices that recur each fortnight — *citayantaḥ*, reminding, informing you. Such as you are, for *jīvātave*, for our long living, *prataram*, more excellently, *sādhaya*, accomplish *dhiyaḥ*, our rites such as the Agnihotra. The rest as before."

*Grammar tail:* *citayantaḥ* — root *citī saṃjñāne*; since the rule of guṇa after a name-sense is not constant, no *guṇa* of the light penultimate. *parvaṇā-parvaṇā* — doubling in the sense of repetition by *nityavīpsayoḥ*; the second member being *āmreḍita*, by *anudāttaṃ ca* it is unaccented. *prataram* — from *pra* with *tarap*, in the sense of excellence of action, the suffix *amu* in Chandas (Pā. 5-4-12 [?]).

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 94.4)** *(Kannada)*

*(agne* — O Agni) *idhmam* — (in order to make you blaze) the bundle of faggots; *bharāma* — we gather; *te* — to you; *parvaṇā-parvaṇā* — by the new- and full-moon and other rites (the fortnightly junctures); *citayantaḥ* — making known; *havīṃṣi* — the oblations such as *caru* and *puroḍāśa*; *vayam* — we; *kṛṇavāma* — offer; *jīvātave* — (we) so that we live long; *dhiyaḥ* — (our Agnihotra and other) rites; *prataram* — in a very excellent manner; *sādhaya* — accomplish; *agne* — O Agni; *tava sakhye* — through friendship with you; *vayam* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer any harm.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 94.4** *(Kannada)*

"O Agni, in order to make you blaze, we prepare a bundle of faggots. We offer you oblations such as *caru* and *puroḍāśa*, making known to you the fortnightly junctures by the new- and full-moon and other rites. So that we may live long, accomplish our Agnihotra and other rites in a most excellent manner. Through friendship with you, favour us so that no harm comes to us."

***idhmam*** — *idhmaḥ samindhanāt* (Ni. 8-4 [?]) | "From the root *indh*, which gives the sense 'to kindle', comes *idhma*: that is, the faggot that makes Agni blaze."

***parvaṇā-parvaṇā*** — *parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇāter vā — ardhamāsaparva devānām asmin prīṇantīti* (Ni. 7-20 [?]) | "From the root *pṛ* that gives the sense 'to fill' [again and again], or from *tṛp*, 'to satisfy' —

---

### Page 524 (PDF 539)

*(Running head: left "524", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 15 Sū. 94".)*

*Special Topics of Rik 94.4, continued from p. 523 (Kannada):*

"— from the root *prī* ('to please') or *tṛp* ('to satisfy') the origin of the word *parva* can be told: [the *parvan*, the juncture] is the time at which the deities are gratified by oblations or by praises; one fortnight-juncture; and in the other sense, 'by the new- and full-moon and other rites that are to be performed regularly at the junctures of the new-moon and full-moon times'."

***citayantaḥ*** — *prajñāpayantaḥ* | "Making known; or: 'making known to you the fortnightly junctures, by the rites to be performed at the junctures' — one meaning; or, as Skandasvāmin says, *yajñakarmatvanyāhātmyaṃ vā jñāpayantaḥ* [as read, doubtful [?]]: 'making known the greatness of sacrificial acts and of you'; and so another meaning may be given: 'having understood together the sacrificial rites to be performed at the junctures and your greatness'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 94.4)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*bharāma* — root *ḍubhṛñ bharaṇe*; *laṭ*, first person plural; since it stands at the head of the pāda, no *nighāta*; since *śap* and the *lasārvadhātuka* are unaccented, the accent of the root remains.
*citayantaḥ* — root *citī saṃjñāne*, of the *curādi* class; by *satyāpapāśa…* (Pā. 3-1-25 [?]) the suffix *ṇic* in its own sense; by the paribhāṣā *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ* the guṇa of the light penultimate because of *ṇic* does not occur; by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* the *ṇic*-ending stem has the name of a root; then *śatṛ* in the present sense; because of *ṇic* the guṇa [*e*] of the root's *ṇi* and the *ay* replacement: *citayat*; the nominative plural; the *ṇic* accent remains.
*parvaṇā-parvaṇā* — by *nityavīpsayoḥ* (Pā. 8-1-4 [?]) the doubling, where repetition is shown; by *tasya paramāmreḍitam* (Pā. 8-1-2 [?]) the second member receives the name *āmreḍita*; by *anudāttaṃ ca* (Pā. 8-1-3 [?]) the *āmreḍita* is unaccented.
*prataram* — *tarap* after *pra*, showing excellence of action; by *amu ca chandasi* (Pā. 5-4-12 [?]) the suffix *amu* after the *tarap*-ending word in the Saṃhitā.
*sādhaya* — root *ṣidhu saṃrāddhau*; since the instigator's action is shown, *ṇic*; by *siddhyater apāralaukike* (Pā. 6-1-49 [?]) the *ā* in the root because of *ṇic*; *loṭ*, second person singular; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*. ‖ 4 ‖
