> विशां गोपा अस्य चरन्ति जन्तवो द्विपच्च यदुत चतुष्पदक्तुभिः ।
> चित्रः प्रकेत उषसो महाँ अस्यग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ ५ ॥

*viśāṃ gopā asya caranti jantavo dvipac ca yad uta catuṣpad aktubhiḥ | citraḥ praketa uṣaso mahām̐ asy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.5)**

> विशाम् । गोपाः । अस्य । चरन्ति । जन्तवः । द्विऽपत् । च । यत् । उत । चतुःऽपत् । अक्तुऽभिः ।
> चित्रः । प्रऽकेतः । उषसः । महान् । असि । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ ५ ॥

*viśām | gopāḥ | asya | caranti | jantavaḥ | dvi-pat | ca | yat | uta | catuḥ-pat | aktu-bhiḥ | citraḥ | pra-ketaḥ | uṣasaḥ | mahān | asi | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.5)**

> अस्याग्नेर्जन्तवो जाता रश्मयो विशां सर्वेषां प्राणिनां गोपा गोपायितारो रक्षकाः सन्तश्चरन्ति । उद्गच्छन्ति । तदनन्तरं यच्च द्विपाद्द्विपात् मनुष्यादिकमस्ति उतापि च चतुष्पात् चतुष्पात् गवादिकं यदस्ति तदुभयमुक्तैर्भूरञ्जकैः रश्मिभिरक्तमाश्लिष्टमभूत् । हे अग्ने चित्रो विचित्रदीप्तियुक्तः प्रकेतो रात्र्यन्धकारावृतानां सर्वेषां प्रज्ञापयिता प्रदर्शयितोषसः उषोदेवतायाः अपि महान् गुणैरधिकोऽसि भवसि । उषास्तु रात्रेश्चरमभागे प्रकाशयति । अग्निस्तु सर्वस्यां रात्रौ प्रकाशयतीति तस्य गुणाधिक्यं । गोपाः । गुपू रक्षणे । गुपूधूपविच्छीत्यायप्रत्ययः । पा. ३-१-२८ [?] । अस्मात्क्विप् । आतो लोपः । वेरपृक्तस्य । लोपाद्वलि लोपो बलीयानिति पूर्वं वलि लोपः । न चातो लोपस्य स्थानि-वत्त्वं । न पदान्तेत्यादिना यलोपं प्रति तन्निषेधात् । द्विपात् । द्वौ पादावस्येति बहुव्रीहौ संख्यासुपूर्वस्येति । पा. ५-४-१४० [?] । पादशब्दस्यान्त्यलोपः समासान्तः । अयस्मयादित्वेन भत्त्वे पादः पत् । पा. ६-४-१३० [?] । इति पद्भावः । एकदेशविकृतस्यान्यत्वात् । परि. ४२ [?] । द्वित्रिभ्यां पाद्दन्मूर्धसु । पा. ६-२-१९७ [?] । इत्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । चतुष्पात् । पूर्ववत्समासान्तः पद्भावश्च । इदुदुपधस्य चाप्रत्ययस्येति विसर्जनीयस्य षत्वं । द्र्यः संख्याययोः । पा. ५-२-३५ [?] इति चतुर्शब्द आद्युदात्तः । स एव बहुव्रीहिस्वरेण शिष्यते ॥

*asyāgner jantavo jātā raśmayo viśāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ gopā gopāyitāro rakṣakāḥ santaś caranti | udgacchanti | tadanantaraṃ yac ca dvipād dvipāt manuṣyādikam asti utāpi ca catuṣpāt catuṣpāt gavādikaṃ yad asti tad ubhayam uktair bhūrañjakaiḥ raśmibhir aktam āśliṣṭam abhūt | he agne citro vicitradīptiyuktaḥ praketo rātryandhakārāvṛtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prajñāpayitā pradarśayitoṣasaḥ uṣodevatāyāḥ api mahān guṇair adhiko 'si bhavasi | uṣās tu rātreś caramabhāge prakāśayati | agnis tu sarvasyāṃ rātrau prakāśayatīti tasya guṇādhikyaṃ | gopāḥ | gupū rakṣaṇe | gupūdhūpavicchīty āyapratyayaḥ | Pā. 3-1-28 [?] | asmāt kvip | āto lopaḥ | ver apṛktasya | lopād vali lopo balīyān iti pūrvaṃ vali lopaḥ | na cāto lopasya sthānivattvaṃ | na padāntety ādinā yalopaṃ prati tanniṣedhāt | dvipāt | dvau pādāv asya iti bahuvrīhau saṃkhyāsupūrvasyeti | Pā. 5-4-140 [?] pādaśabdasyāntyalopaḥ samāsāntaḥ | ayasmayādi­tvena bhattve pādaḥ pat | Pā. 6-4-130 [?] iti padbhāvaḥ | ekadeśavikṛtasyānyatvāt | Pari. 42 [?] | dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrdhasu | Pā. 6-2-197 [?] ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | catuṣpāt | pūrvavat samāsāntaḥ padbhāvaś ca | idudupadhasya cāpratyayasyeti visarjanīyasya ṣatvaṃ | dryaḥ saṃkhyāyayoḥ | Pā. 5-2-35 [?] iti catur­śabda ādyudāttaḥ | sa eva bahuvrīhisvareṇa śiṣyate ‖*

*Translation:* "*Asya*, of this Agni, *jantavaḥ* — the born ones, the rays — *viśām gopāḥ* — protectors, guardians, of all beings — *caranti*, go forth. Thereafter *dvipat*, whatever biped there is, men and the like; *uta ca catuṣpat*, and whatever quadruped there is, cows and the like — both of these *aktubhiḥ*, by the rays which colour the earth, become coloured, touched. O Agni, *citraḥ*, of varied lustre, *praketaḥ*, the one who makes known, shows, all that is enveloped in the darkness of night, you are *mahān*, great, superior in qualities, even than *uṣasaḥ*, the goddess Uṣas: for Uṣas shines in the last part of the night; but Agni shines through the whole night: that is his superiority in quality."

*Grammar tail (characterized):* *gopāḥ* — root *gupū rakṣaṇe*; the suffix *āya* by *gupūdhūpavicchi…* (Pā. 3-1-28 [?]); *kvip* after it; elision of the *ā*; since the *kvip* is *apṛkta* its elision takes place first; *dvipāt* — in the *bahuvrīhi* "of which there are two feet", *pāda* loses its final by *saṃkhyāsupūrvasya* (Pā. 5-4-140 [?]); *pad* for *pāda* by *padbhāva* (Pā. 6-4-130 [?]); the final-acute by *dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrdhasu* (Pā. 6-2-197 [?]). *catuṣpāt* — as before, with *ṣatva* of the visarga; the initial-acute of *catur* by *dryaḥ…* (Pā. 5-2-35 [?], numerals doubtful); that accent remains by the *bahuvrīhi* accent.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 94.5)** *(Kannada; continues on p. 526)*

### Page 526 (PDF 541)

*(Running head: left "526", centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", right "Ma. 1 A. 15 Sū. 94".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Rik 94.5)** *(Kannada)*

*asya* — this Agni's; *jantavaḥ* — rays; *viśām* — (of all) living beings; *gopāḥ* — as protectors; *caranti* — spread; *yat* — whichever; *dvipat* — beings with two feet, men and the like; *uta* — and; *catuṣpat ca* — beings with four feet, cows and the like also; *aktubhiḥ* — by the rays (of this Agni), they gain consciousness; *agne* — O Agni; *citraḥ* — of varied lustre; *praketaḥ* — making all [that is enveloped in darkness] bright; *uṣasaḥ* — than the Uṣas deity; *mahān asi* — you are superior; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayam* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not be afflicted by harm.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha of Rik 94.5** *(Kannada)*

"The rays of this Agni spread all around as protectors of all beings. Those with two feet, men and the like, and those with four feet, cows and the like, gain consciousness by the rays of this Agni. O Agni, you are of varied lustre, illuminating all the world covered by darkness, and are superior in greatness even to the Uṣas deity who shines only by day [read: at the close of night]. Through friendship with you, may we be afflicted by no harm of any kind."

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source; Rik 94.5)*

"His genial (flames), the preservers of mankind, spread around and both bipeds and quadrupeds are enlivened by his rays ; Shining with various lustre, and illuminating (the world by night) you are superior to the dawn ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship." — as printed.

**॥ विशेषविषयगळु ॥ — Special Topics (Rik 94.5)** *(Kannada)*

***viśām*** — "*manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ* and the like being read among the twenty-five names of men (Ni. 2-[?]), it means 'men'; but here it should be explained as *sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām*, 'of all living beings'."

### Page 527 (PDF 542)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 31 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 527.)*

*Special Topics of Rik 94.5, continued from p. 526 (Kannada):*

***jantavaḥ*** — *jātāḥ raśmayaḥ* | "'The rays born of Agni': the rays of Agni that have arisen from him. This word, like the words *jantu*, *jantavaḥ*, *jantubhiḥ*, is used as an epithet in the Ṛksaṃhitā, suiting the context for whatever kind of born thing may be meant: ṛtviks, sacrificers, enemies, all creatures and so on, so that the sense is taken to apply to all things possessed of birth in the various contexts (see Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?]; 1-[?]-3 [?]; 3-[?]-2 [?]; 6-[?]-[?] [?]; 10-[?]-4 [?] and so on)."

***aktubhiḥ*** — "*śyāvī, kṣapā, śarvarī, aktuḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-two names of night (Ni. 1-[?]); in many places the word *aktu* means 'night'. But in some contexts the word is used in the senses of 'ray', 'weapon', 'darkness', and so on. Since the root *añj* has the senses of 'cover', 'anoint', 'be bright' and so on, the meanings 'darkness that anoints', 'rays that cover everything', 'night that is dark', 'weapon that covers the body' arise. For example, for the word *aktu* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?], they explain 'weapon'; for the word in Ṛk 3-[?]-3 [?], 'darkness'; but in most places the meaning is 'night'."

"If in this Ṛk the meaning 'night' is taken, one kind of construction arises; if 'rays', another. According to Skandasvāmin: *aktubhiḥ — rātrināmaitat | iha tu sāhacaryād annaṃcareṣu rakṣaḥpiśācādiṣu vartate | rātricaraiḥ saha ity arthaḥ* — '*aktu* is a name of night; but here, by association, it refers to those who move at night, such as the Rākṣasas and Piśācas: the meaning is 'together with the night-wanderers''. Since *aktu* is read among the names of night, it ought to mean 'night'; but here, by association, it is explained that all living beings, men and the rest, are known with the night-wandering Rākṣasas, Piśācas and others. Hence *uṣasaḥ (api) mahān asi* — 'you are superior even to the goddess Uṣas': Uṣas shines only in the last part of the night, making the beings of the world visible; but you, making everything visible throughout the night, are therefore superior to Uṣas. Sāyaṇa's explanation: 'all bipeds, men and the like, and quadrupeds, cows and the like, are made known by the covering rays [*aktubhiḥ*]'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 94.5)** *(Kannada; grammar page, noted briefly)*

*gopāḥ* — root *gupū rakṣaṇe*; by *gupūdhūpavicchipaṇipanibhya āyaḥ* (Pā. 3-1-28 [?]) the suffix *āya* in its own sense; by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* the *āya*-ending stem takes the name of a root, since *āya* belongs to the *sanādi* group; after it the suffix *kvip*; by *ato lopaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-48 [?]) the *a* of the root-stem is elided because of it —

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.5, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly):*

[*gopāḥ*, continued —] "…for the *v* of *kvip*, which stands after it and is *apṛkta*, the elision should be done; but first, by the statement *ver apṛktasya* and *lopād vali lopo balīyān* — 'the elision before *val* is stronger than the elision [of *a*]' — by *lopo vyor vali* (Pā. 6-1-66 [?]) the *y* is elided because of the *v*. When the *y* is elided, it might be doubted that the *ā* does not have the status of the replaced [*sthānivadbhāva*]; but by *na padāntadvirvacana…* (Pā. 1-1-58 [?]) the *sthānivadbhāva* is prohibited in the matter of *y*-elision. Thereafter, by *ver apṛktasya* (Pā. 6-1-67 [?]) the elision of the *v* of *kvip*. The word *gopā* ends in *ā*."
*caranti* — root *cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*; *laṭ*, third person plural; since it follows a word, the *nighāta*.
*dvipāt* — "*dvau pādāv asya*"; in the *bahuvrīhi*, by *saṃkhyāsupūrvasya* (Pā. 5-4-140 [?]), since a numeral stands before, the final of *pāda* is elided, as a *samāsānta*; by *ayasmayādīni chandasi* (Pā. 1-4-20 [?]) it receives the name *bha*, and by *pādaḥ pat* (Pā. 6-4-130 [?]) the replacement *pad*; since in *pāt* only the short [*pad*] has come, by the paribhāṣā *ekadeśavikṛtam ananyavat* it is treated as *pād* itself; by *dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrdhasu* (Pā. 6-2-197 [?]) the final member takes the final-acute.
*catuṣpāt* — as before, since it is a compound, the *samāsānta* elision and the *padbhāva*; when *catur + pat* stands, by *idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya* the visarga takes *ṣatva*.
*catuḥ* — by *nraḥ saṃkhyāyāḥ* (Phiṭ-sūtra 2-[?] [?]) numerals ending in *n* and *r* take the initial-acute; since *catur* ends in *r*, it takes the initial-acute; by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* the same accent remains in the compound. ‖ 5 ‖

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "… 'one of favourable conduct'. Or: in all rites you are placed in the Āhavanīya fire in the eastern quarter. Or, the *purohita* is the Brahman priest, as the deputy of Bṛhaspati, the *purohita* of the gods. And as another mantra has it: 'Bṛhaspati is the Brahman of the gods, I of men.' So, abiding in the Brahman as before and taking that form, you, being learned in all the priestly duties — the Adhvaryu duties and the rest — O wise Agni, you cause the rite to thrive: you perform them complete, without lack or excess. Grammatical tail: *januṣā* from *jan* with the Uṇādi suffix *usi*; *purohitaḥ* from *dadhāti* with the participial suffix (*niṣṭhā*) in the passive, the *si* suffix and the word *pur(s)* as read, final-acute; *puras* as an indeclinable by the rule on *taddhita* and non-all-case-endings, a *gati* by 'puro 'vyayam', hence the accent of the prior member by 'gatir anantaraḥ'; *ārtvijyā* with *ṣyañ* by the *brāhmaṇādi* group, first-vowel acute through the *ñ*-marker. *(The print of the grammatical tail is clotted in places; the sūtra numbers are not legible at this size and are not supplied; one clause after "si-pratyayā" is lost in the print [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"(*agne*) — O Agni; *tvam* — you; *adhvaryuḥ* — (in the sacrifice) the Adhvaryu, or the performer of the ordained rites; *uta* — and; *pūrvyaḥ* — principal; *hotā* — as Hotṛ, (or the one who gives the invocation to the gods); *asi* — you are; *praśāstā* — (in the sacrificial act) the one who gives instruction to all, or the one in the Maitrāvaruṇa station; *potā* — (the purifier of the sacrifice, or the one who completes the rite) as Potṛ; *januṣā* — by nature; *purohitaḥ* — one whose conduct is favourable to those who come later in heaven and the like, or the *purohita* of the gods; *viśvā* — all; *ārtvijyā* — the duties of the priests; *vidvān* — knowing; *dhīra* — O wise one; *agne* — O Agni; *puṣyasi* — (without the least lack or excess) you bring the sacrifice to completion with all its parts; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayaṃ* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer harm."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Agni, you are in the sacrifice the Adhvaryu, the principal Hotṛ, one who occupies the Maitrāvaruṇa station and the Potṛ station, and by nature the *purohita*. Being wise, you know the duties of all the priests, and so bring the sacrifice to completion with all its parts, without the least lack or fault. Because of friendship with you, may we suffer no harm."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> You are the sacrificing or the invoking priest, you are the principal (presenter of the offering) the director ( of the ceremonies ), their performer *(continues on p. 531)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Kannada)**

***adhvaryu, hotṛ, praśāstṛ, purohita*** — "The varieties of priests named in 'adhvaryu, hotṛ, praśāstṛ, purohita…' have been explained in detail in earlier volumes. Since Agni, the god, is the king of the rites (*adhvara*), since he bears the whole burden of carrying them through, since he invites the gods so that they come to the sacrifice, since he makes the offered oblation into portions, and since he supplies to the gods and to the sacrificers, each according to their wish, the fruits that satisfy them, he is praised in the words *viśvā ārtvijyā vidvān dhīra agne puṣyasi* — that he knows well the duties of all the priests and carries the sacrifice through in full without the least lack or excess."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

*hotā* — root *hu* (giving, eating), suffix *tṛn* in the agent sense, guṇa of the root; initial acute by *ñnityādir nityam*. *praśāstā* — root *śās* (instruct), suffix *tṛc*, final acute by *cit*-ness. *januṣā* — root *jan* (to be born), Uṇādi suffix *usi*; the *u* acute by the suffix accent. *puroḥitaḥ* — *dhāñ* (holding, nourishing) with *kta*, replaced by *hi* by *dadhāter hiḥ* (Pā. [?]); *pur* by the suffix *asi* in the sense of *pūrvādharāvarāṇām asipuradhavaś caiṣām* (Pā. [?]), giving the word *puras*, final-acute; indeclinable status by *taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ* (Pā. 1-1-38 [?]) and *puro 'vyayam* (Pā. 1-4-67 [?]); *gati* status, hence the accent of the first member by *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. 6-2-49 [?]); the *o* of *puroḥitaḥ* acute. *viśvā* — neuter plural: *śi* in place of *śas*, elided by *śeś chandasi bahulam*. *ārtvijyā* — "the priest's (rites)": by inclusion in the *brāhmaṇa* group, *ṣyañ* by *guṇavacanabrāhmaṇādibhyaḥ karmaṇi ca* (Pā. 5-1-124 [?]); vṛddhi of the first vowel by *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ*; *ṛ* turned to *ra* as read; initial acute by *ñit*; elision of *śi* as before. *vidvān* — root *vid* (to know), *śatṛ* in the sense of the present, replaced by *vasu* by *vido laṭo vā* / *vide śatur vasuḥ* (Pā. 3-2-[?] [?]); the stem *vidvas*; the nominative *su* following, lengthening of the vowel by *sāv anantasya*; *num* augment by *ugit*-ness; elision of *su* by *hal ṅyābbhyaḥ…*, elision of the final consonant by *saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ*. *(Grammar page, noted briefly; the sūtra numbers are small and were not chased; those shown are as read, doubtful.)*

### Sūkta 94, Rik 7 (continued; printed pp. 533–535)

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.7)** *(Jagatī; accent marks printed here, not reproduced)*

> यो विश्वतः सुप्रतीकः सदृङ्ङसि दूरे चित्सन्तळिदिवाति रोचसे ।
> रात्र्याश्चिदन्धोऽति देव पश्यस्यग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ ७ ॥

*yo viśvataḥ supratīkaḥ sadṛṅṅasi dūre cit san taḷid ivāti rocase | rātryāś cid andho 'ti deva paśyasy agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.7)**

> यः । विश्वतः । सुऽप्रतीकः । सऽदृक् । असि । दूरे । चित् । सन् ।
> तळित्ऽइव । अति । रोचसे ।
> रात्र्याः । चित् । अन्धः । अति । देव । पश्यसि । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ ७ ॥

*yaḥ | viśvataḥ | su-pratīkaḥ | sa-dṛk | asi | dūre | cit | san | taḷit-iva | ati | rocase | rātryāḥ | cit | andhaḥ | ati | deva | paśyasi | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.7)**

> हे अग्ने यस्त्वं सुप्रतीकः शोभनाङ्गः सन् विश्वतः सर्वस्मादपि सदृङ्ङसि अस्मानः [?] सदृशो भवसि । सत्वं दूरे चित्सन् दूरेऽपि वर्तमानः सन् तळिदिव । अन्तिकनामैतत् । अन्तिके वर्तमान इवाति रोचसे । अतिशयेन दीप्यसे । तदुक्तं यास्केन । दूरेऽपि सन्नन्तिक इव सन्दृश्यसे । नि. ३-१० [?] इति । रात्र्याश्चित् रात्रेरपि रात्रेः संबन्धिनमन्धो बहुलमन्धकारमपि हे देव द्योतमानाग्ने इति पश्यसि । अतीत्य प्रकाशसे । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ सुप्रतीकः । शोभनं प्रतीकोऽङ्गं यस्य । क्रत्वादयश्चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । सदृङ् । समानान्ययोश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । पा. ३-२-६० [?] इति समानोऽपपदाद्दृशेः क्विन् । दृग्दृशवतुषु । पा. ६-३-८९ [?] इति समानस्य सभावः । दृक्स्वःस्वतवसां छन्दसि । पा. ६-१-८३ [?] इति नुम् । संयोगान्तलोपः । क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः । कुत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । रात्र्याः । रात्रेश्चाजसौ । पा. सू. ४-१-३१ [?] इति ङीप् ॥

*he agne yas tvaṃ supratīkaḥ śobhanāṅgaḥ san viśvataḥ sarvasmād api sadṛṅṅasi asmānaḥ [?] sadṛśo bhavasi | sa tvaṃ dūre cit san dūre 'pi vartamānaḥ san taḷid iva | antikanāmaitat | antike vartamāna ivāti rocase | atiśayena dīpyase | tad uktaṃ yāskena | dūre 'pi sann antika iva sandṛśyase | ni. 3-10 [?] iti | rātryāś cit rātre api rātreḥ saṃbandhinam andho bahulam andhakāram api he deva dyotamānāgne iti paśyasi | atītya prakāśase | anyat pūrvavat ‖ supratīkaḥ | śobhanaṃ pratīko 'ṅgaṃ yasya | kratvādayaś cety uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | sadṛṅ | samānānyayoś ceti vaktavyam | pā. 3-2-60 [?] iti samāno 'papadād dṛśeḥ kvin | dṛgdṛśavatuṣu | pā. 6-3-89 [?] iti samānasya sabhāvaḥ | dṛksvaḥsvatavasāṃ chandasi | pā. 6-1-83 [?] iti num | saṃyogāntalopaḥ | kvinpratyayasya kuḥ | kutvaṃ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | rātryāḥ | rātreś cājasau | pā. sū. 4-1-31 [?] iti ṅīp ‖*

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "O Agni, you who, being of fair limbs (*supratīka*), are *sadṛk* from every side — like to us [the word as printed is doubtful, [?]] — though you are far off, you shine surpassingly as if near (*taḷit* is a word for 'near'). This was said by Yāska: 'Though far off, you are seen as if near' (Nirukta, numeral as read [?]). *rātryāś cit* — even of the night, you see (*paśyasi*) even the great darkness belonging to the night, O shining god, and shine beyond it. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: *supratīka* — fair limbs; the first member of the compound gets the acute on its first syllable by *kratvādayaś ca*; *sadṛk* — *dṛś* with *samāna* in the preceding position, *kvin*, *sa*-substitution for *samāna*, *num* augment in the Veda, loss of the conjunct final, *ku*-substitution for the *kvin* suffix; accent of the earlier member in a *kṛdanta* compound; *rātryāḥ* — *ṅīp* by the rule on *rātri*. *(The bhāṣya of this Rik is clotted at* asmānaḥ*, and the sūtra numbers read from small figures are doubtful [?]; the print's* nuṃ *is read from the Kannada note on p. 535, the bhāṣya's own letter being* suṃ*-like [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*agne* — O Agni; *yaḥ* — you who; *supratīkaḥ* — of beautiful, lovely limbs; *viśvataḥ* — in all directions; *sadṛk asi* — are (without the least difference) equal in appearance (such a one are you); *dūre cit san* — though far away, also; *taḷid iva* — as if near; *ati rocase* — you shine exceedingly; *deva* — O shining Agni, (you); *rātryāḥ cit andhaḥ* — even the darkness of the time of night; *ati paśyasi* — piercing it, you shine; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayaṃ* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer harm."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Agni, you, being of lovely form, are of one aspect in every direction, without the least difference. Though far off, you shine as if near. By your radiance you pierce even the darkness of the night and shine. Because of friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> You are of graceful form and alike on every side, and although remote, shine as if near ; O divine Agni, you can see beyond the darkness of night ; Agni, let us not suffer jinury [sic] through your friendship.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Kannada)**

***supratīkaḥ*** — *śobhanamukhaḥ*: "*śobhanamukhaḥ*, 'one of lovely face'. 'One with a charming face'; this epithet is used very commonly of Agni, Sūrya, Uṣas, and in the main in connection with them; they are said to be those whose form is endowed with lustre, *(continues on p. 535)*"

"…so the epithets *supratīkaḥ* and *susandṛśaḥ* are found much used in their regard."

***taḷit*** — "*taḷit, āsāt, ambaram* — among the eleven last names read in the list of words, which in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-9 [?]) mean 'near': 'in the vicinity'. That is, Agni, though far off, shines as lovely as if near, in his great radiance."

***andhaḥ*** — "*tamo 'sy andha ucyate nāsmin dhyānaṃ bhavati na darśanam andhatama ity abhibhāṣante* [as read, doubtful [?]]" — Ni. 3-1 [?]:

> तमोऽस्यन्ध उच्यते नास्मिन् ध्यानं भवति न दर्शनमन्धन्तम इत्यभिभाषन्ते ।
> *tamo 'sy andha ucyate nāsmin dhyānaṃ bhavati na darśanam andhantama ity abhibhāṣante |*

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "Darkness is called* andha*: in it there is no seeing and no sight; they say 'the blindest dark'." The Kannada adds:)* "Because one cannot look, or cannot go forward, in it. The word *andha* means 'darkness'. The expression of the people, 'it is dark (blinding) darkness', is well known."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

*viśvataḥ* — to the word *viśva* in the ablative sense the suffix *tasil* by *pañcamyās tasil* (Pā. [?]); acute on the syllable before the suffix by the *lit* rule. *supratīkaḥ* — "the one whose limb (*pratīka*) is lovely"; the first member's accent per *kratvādayaś ca* (the later member gets the initial acute). *sadṛk* — root *dṛś* (seeing) when the word *samāna* is the upapada, *kvin* by *samānānyayoś ceti vaktavyam* (Pā. 3-2-60 [?]); *sa*-substitution of *samāna* by *dṛgdṛśavatuṣu* (Pā. 6-3-89 [?]); *sadṛś*; then, with *su* following, *nuṃ* by *dṛk-svaḥ-svatavasāṃ chandasi* (Pā. 6-1-83 [?]); *saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ* removes the *ś*; the elision of *su* to be stated by *hal-ṅyābbhyo…*; *ku*-substitution (*kvin*'s *n* → *ṅ*) by *kuṃ…* (Pā. 8-2-62 [?]); form *sadṛṅ*; accent by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (the *kṛt* member). *asi* — root *as* (to be), *ādādi* class, *laṭ* second person singular *sip*, *tāsasty or lopaḥ* removes the *s* of the root (Pā. 7-4-50 [?]); the *nighāta* accent does not arise since the verb is joined by *yad*; *sip* being *pit* is unaccented; the root's accent remains. *rātryāḥ* — *rātri* is a feminine stem in *i*; *ṅas*/*ṅi* by *rātreś cājasau* (Pā. 4-1-31 [?]) takes *ṅīp*; a variant of the genitive singular. ‖ 7 ‖ *(Grammar page, noted briefly.)*

### Sūkta 94, Rik 8 (printed pp. 536–538)

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.8)** *(Jagatī; accent marks printed here, not reproduced)*

> पूर्वो देवा भवतु सुन्वतो रथोऽस्माकं शंसो अभ्यस्तु दूढ्यः ।
> तदा जानीतोत पुष्यता वचोऽग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ ८ ॥

*pūrvo devā bhavatu sunvato ratho 'smākaṃ śaṃso abhy astu dūḍhyaḥ | tadā jānītota puṣyatā vaco 'gne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.8)**

> पूर्वः । देवाः । भवतु । सुन्वतः । रथः । अस्माकम् । शंसः । अभि । अस्तु । दुःऽध्यः ।
> तत् । आ । जानीत । उत । पुष्यत । वचः । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ ८ ॥

*pūrvaḥ | devāḥ | bhavatu | sunvataḥ | rathaḥ | asmākam | śaṃsaḥ | abhi | astu | duḥ-dhyaḥ | tat | ā | jānīta | uta | puṣyata | vacaḥ | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 8 ‖*

*(Reading note: the Saṃhitā has* dūḍhyaḥ *where the Pada has* duḥ-dhyaḥ*, and* puṣyatā *where the Pada has* puṣyata*, as printed. The Pada's* duḥ-dhyaḥ *is as the print gives it.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.8)**

> हे देवा अग्न्यवयवभूताः सर्वे देवाः सुन्वतः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वतो यजमानस्य रथः पूर्वः अन्येषामयजमानानां रथेभ्यो मुख्यो भवतु । अपि चास्माकं शंसः शंसनीयमभिशापरूपं पापं दूढ्यो दुर्धियः पापबुद्धेस्तस्य [?]दनिष्टाचरणपरान् शत्रूनभ्यस्तु । अभिभवतु । [?] तदिदं मद्वाक्यं हे देवा आ जानीत । अभिमुखेनावगच्छत । उताऽपि च तन्मद्वचोऽस्मदीयं वचनं शदर्थाचरणेन [?] पुष्यत । प्रवर्धयत । हे सर्वदेवात्मकाग्ने सख्ये इत्यादि पूर्ववत् ॥ सुन्वतः । शतुरनुमो [?] इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । शंसः । शंस्यते कीर्त्यते इति शंसोऽभिशापः । कर्मणि घञ् । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । दूढ्यः । दुष्टं ध्यायन्तीति दुर्धियः । ध्यै चिन्तायामित्यस्मात् क्विप्चेति क्विप् । दृशिग्रहणानुवृत्तेस्तस्य च विध्यन्तरोपसंग्रहार्थत्वात् संप्रसारणं । पृषोदरादिषु ध्यै चेति पाठाद्दुरो रेफस्योत्वं उत्तरपदादेः ढत्वं [?] च ॥

*he devā agnyavayavabhūtāḥ sarve devāḥ sunvataḥ somābhiṣavaṃ kurvato yajamānasya rathaḥ pūrvaḥ anyeṣām ayajamānānāṃ rathebhyo mukhyo bhavatu | api cāsmākaṃ śaṃsaḥ śaṃsanīyam abhiśāparūpaṃ pāpaṃ dūḍhyo durdhiyaḥ pāpabuddhes tasya [?]daniṣṭācaraṇaparān śatrūn abhy astu | abhibhavatu | [?] tad idaṃ madvākyaṃ he devā ā jānīta | abhimukhenāvagacchata | utāpi ca tan madvaco 'smadīyaṃ vacanaṃ śadarthācaraṇena [?] puṣyata | pravardhayata | he sarvadevātmakāgne sakhye ity ādi pūrvavat ‖ sunvataḥ | śatur anumo [?] iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | śaṃsaḥ | śaṃsyate kīrtyate iti śaṃso 'bhiśāpaḥ | karmaṇi ghañ | ñittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | dūḍhyaḥ | duṣṭaṃ dhyāyantīti durdhiyaḥ | dhyai cintāyām ity asmāt kvip ceti kvip | dṛśigrahaṇānuvṛtteḥ tasya ca vidhyantaropasaṃgrahārthatvāt saṃprasāraṇaṃ | pṛṣodarādiṣu dhyai ceti pāṭhād duro repha syottvaṃ uttarapadāder ḍhatvaṃ [?] ca ‖*

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "O gods, all you who are the members of Agni: let the chariot of the sacrificer who presses the Soma be foremost, chief above the chariots of the other, non-sacrificing, men. And let our *śaṃsa* — the praiseworthy (that is, curse-like) 'sin' — overwhelm our enemies, who are evil-minded and bent on doing us harm. Understand this word of mine, O gods; apprehend it as it faces you; and make this speech of mine thrive by acting in accord with it. O Agni, who are the self of all gods — as before." Grammatical tail: *sunvataḥ* (the case-ending acute by the rule on *śatṛ* without *num*, numeral and wording as read, doubtful [?]); *śaṃsaḥ* — *ghañ* in the passive of *śaṃsu*, first-syllable acute by the *ñ*; *dūḍhyaḥ* — *durdhiyaḥ*, *kvip* after *dhyai*, *saṃprasāraṇa*; by the *pṛṣodarādi* group the *r* of *dur* is lengthened with *u* and the initial *dh* of the second member becomes *ḍh* (as read, doubtful [?]). *(The bhāṣya of this Rik is clotted at several places: the word after "pāpabuddhes tasya", the clause after "abhibhavatu" and "śadarthācaraṇena"; marked [?] and read as given.)*

### Page 537 (PDF 552)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 31 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 537.)*

*(The grammatical tail of the bhāṣya, begun on p. 536, ends at the head of this page as transcribed above.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*devāḥ* — O gods (who are the limbs of Agni), all of you; *sunvataḥ* — of the sacrificer who presses the Soma-juice; *rathaḥ* — the chariot; *pūrvaḥ* — ahead of (all the others'); *bhavatu* — may it be; *asmākaṃ* — our; *śaṃsaḥ* — the blame-like undesired thing, the 'sin'; *dūḍhyaḥ* — the evil-minded enemies; *abhyastu* — may it harm; *tat* — this (my) hymn; *ā jānīta* — understand well, apprehend; *uta* — and; *vacaḥ* — my prayer; *puṣyata* — fulfil; *agne* — O Agni; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayaṃ* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not be harmed."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O gods, all of you are limbs of Agni. By your grace let the chariot of the sacrificer who presses the Soma-juice go ahead of all others'. May our blame-like undesired thing harm the enemies of sinful mind. Understand well this hymn of mine, and all of you fulfil my prayer. O Agni, through friendship with you may we suffer no harm of any kind."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Gods, let the chariot of the offerer of the libation be foremost ; let our, denunciations overwhelm the wicked : understand and fulfil my words ; Agnil [sic] let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Kannada)**

***dūḍhyaḥ*** — *durdhiyaḥ* (Ni. 3-? [?], numeral as read "३-२" [?]): "evil-minded, of sinful thought — our enemies who speak ill and are inclined to sin; that is the sense."

***śaṃsaḥ*** — *abhiśāparūpaṃ pāpam*: "the blame-like sin: may our censuring sin go against and harm our enemies, the sinful ones, and overwhelm them."

***puṣyata*** — *pravardhayata*: "make [it] grow, to the full."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 538)*

*sunvataḥ* — root *ṣuñ* (pressing), *śatṛ* in the present sense; *śnu* as the *vikaraṇa* by *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (as read); *ṣ* → *s* for the root's initial; *sārvadhātukam apit* makes the suffix *ṅit*-like so that *guṇa* does not arise…

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.8, continued** *(grammar, noted briefly)*: for the *śatṛ* and the *śnu*, *guṇa* does not arise because of the *jñ*-type *ṅit*-ness as printed. *sunvat* is the stem; the genitive singular (the fourth-case form as read) has the case-ending acute by *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-[?] [?]; the stem lacks *num* and the ending begins with a vowel). *śaṃsaḥ* — root *śaṃsu* (praise); *ghañ* in the passive sense; *ñ*-ness gives the first syllable acute by *ñnityādir nityam*. *dūḍhyaḥ* — "they think ill": root *dhyai* (thinking), *kvip* by *kvip ca*; here the *dṛś*-heading is carried forward by *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate* (Pā. 3-2-178 [?]) so that the rule applies to this root also, and *saṃprasāraṇa* arises; by the reading *dhyai ca* in the *pṛṣodarādi* group, the *r* of *dur* before it and the *dh* of the root take the changes noted in the bhāṣya. *jānīta* — root *jñā* (knowing), *loṭ* second person plural, *ta*-substitution; *jā* for *jñā* by *jñājanor jā* (Pā. 7-3-79 [?]); *śnā* by *kryādibhyaḥ śnā*; *ī* for *śnā* before a consonant-initial ending by *īhalyaghoḥ* (Pā. 6-4-113 [?]); it takes *nighāta* accent (following a word that is not a verb [?]). *puṣyata* — root *puṣa* (thriving), *divādi*, *loṭ* second person plural; *tiṅanta*, *nighāta* accent; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā (*puṣyatā*) by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* (as read). ‖ 8 ‖ *(Grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers small and doubtful [?].)*

*he agne tvaṃ vadhair hananasādhanair āyudhair duḥśaṃsān duḥkhena kīrtanīyān dūḍhyo durdhiyaḥ pāpabuddhīn api jahi | vadhaṃ prāpaya | ye kecit ye ke cana dūre viprakṛṣṭadeśe vāntike samīpadeśe vā vartamānā atriṇo 'ttāro rākṣasādayo vidyante tān spardhiyo 'pi [?] jahīty arthaḥ ‖ athānantaraṃ yajñāya yajñapataye gṛṇate tvāṃ stuvate yajamānāya sugaṃ śobhanaṃ mārgaṃ kṛdhi | kuru | anyat pūrvavat ‖ vadhaiḥ | hanaś ca vadha iti hanteḥ karaṇe 'p vadhādeśaś ca | sa cādanto 'ntodāttaḥ | tasyāto lope saty api nivṛttisvareṇa [?] pratyayasyodāttatvaṃ | duḥśaṃsān | īṣadduḥsuṣv iti karmaṇi khal | liti iti pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | jahi | loṭi hiḥ | hanter ja iti jādeśaḥ | tasyāsiddhavad atrābhād ity asiddhatvād dher lugbhāvaḥ [?] | anti | antikasya kādilopo bahulam iti kalopaḥ | atriṇaḥ | ādes trini ceti trinipratyayaḥ | ikāro nakāraparitrāṇārthaḥ | gṛṇate | śatur anuma iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | sugaṃ | sudurorādhikaraṇe | pā. 3-2-48 [?] iti gamer ḍaḥ | kṛdhi | śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasīti her dhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk ‖*

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "O Agni, with your death-dealing weapons strike the evil-speaking ones (those who are hard to speak of), the evil-minded: bring them to death. Whichever eaters (*atriṇaḥ* — ogres and the like) there are, far off or near at hand, strike those as well. Then, for the sacrificer who praises you, the master of the sacrifice, make a fair path. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: *vadhaiḥ* — from *han* in the instrumental sense with *ap* and substitution of *vadha*, ending in *a*, final-acute; *duḥśaṃsān* — *khal* in the passive; *jahi* — *loṭ*, *hi*, *ja* for *han*, with the loss of the *hi* as treated as non-operating [?]; *anti* — from *antika* by loss of *ka*; *atriṇaḥ* — the suffix *trin*, whose *i* is for the preservation of the *n*; *gṛṇate* — case-ending acute; *sugam* — *gam* with *ḍa* after *su*/*dur* in a locative sense; *kṛdhi* — *hi* → *dhi* in the Veda after *kṛ* (the rule on *śru, śṛṇu, pṛ, kṛ, vṛ*), with elision of the *vikaraṇa* (*u*) by *bahulaṃ chandasi*. *(The grammatical tail is clotted at* nivṛttisvareṇa *and* lugbhāvaḥ*; the sūtra numeral is as read, doubtful [?].)*

### Page 540 (PDF 555)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 31 [?]"; centre: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 15 [?], Sūkta 94".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*agne* — O Agni; *vadhaiḥ* — with the weapons that cause death; *duḥśaṃsān* — those known as evil-speaking ones (wicked ones); *dūḍhyaḥ* — the enemies of sinful mind; *apa jahi* — destroy; *ye kecit* — whichever enemies; *dūre* — far off; *vā* — or near at hand; *vā* — whether; *atriṇaḥ* — such rākṣasa-like, evil enemies (destroy); *atha* — then; *yajñāya* — to the sacrificer; *gṛṇate* — (who praises you) the praising one; *sugaṃ* — a lovely path; *kṛdhi* — make; *agne* — O Agni; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayaṃ* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer harm."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Agni, destroy with your death-dealing weapons the evil-minded enemies, known as wicked ones, whether they are far off or near. Destroy our wicked enemies, the ogres. Make a lovely path for the sacrificer, the praiser of you. Through friendship with you, favour us so that we suffer no harm of any kind."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Overcome with your fatal (weapons) the wicked and the impicus [sic], all who are enemies whether distant or near, and then provide an easy ( path ) for the sacrificer who praises you ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics (Kannada)**

***vadhaiḥ*** — *hananasādhanair āyudhaiḥ*: "with weapons that are the means of killing, that is the sense. In the Ṛksaṃhitā in general the word *vadhaiḥ* is used in the sense *vadhasādhanair āyudhaiḥ*. For example —"

> कुत्साय यत्र पुरुहूत वन्वञ्छुष्णमनन्तैः परियासि वधैः ।
> *kutsāya yatra puruhūta vanvañ chuṣṇam anantaiḥ pariyāsi vadhaiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-121-9 as read [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "when, much-invoked one, for Kutsa you go about, smiting Śuṣṇa with unending blows".)*

> स्वयं सो अस्मदा निदो वधैरजेत दुर्मतिम् ।
> *svayaṃ so asmad ā nido vadhair ajeta durmatim |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-129-6 as read [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "may he himself drive from us, with blows, the reviling and the ill-intentioned".)*

"Likewise in 1-133-6; 2-31-2; 6-20-4 [all as read, doubtful [?]] and other Ṛks, the word *vadhaiḥ* is used throughout in the sense of 'means of killing'."

### Page 541 (PDF 556)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 31 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 541.)*

***atriṇaḥ*** — "*attāraḥ, bhakṣitāraś ca*: the devourers, who eat men, or the rākṣasas who rend bellies (the Kannada word as read, doubtful [?])."

***sugaṃ*** — *śobhanaṃ mārgaṃ*: "a lovely path. From the point of view of travel, it means a path that is easily passed along; from the moral point of view, it means the best, the most glorious path. The word is used in both senses. For example —"

> देवयानान् सुगान् पथः कुरुष्व सुमनाः स्वयम् ।
> *devayānān sugān pathaḥ kuruṣva sumanāḥ svayam |*
> (*Bṛhaddevatā* 7-6-5 as read [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "make the god-travelled paths easy to go, yourself of good mind".)* "In this verse the sense is of paths along which the gods travel easily. In the same sense in the Ṛksaṃhitā also:"

> शं नः करत्यर्वते सुगं मेषाय मेष्ये । नृभ्यो नारिभ्यो गवे ॥
> *śaṃ naḥ karaty arvate sugaṃ meṣāya meṣye | nṛbhyo nāribhyo gave ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-43-6 as read [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "may he make welfare and an easy path for our horse, for the ram and the ewe, for men, for women, for the cow".)*

"In this Ṛk, and in Ṛks such as 9-63-10 [?] and 10-?-5 [?], it is said to be an easily traversed path; and in the sense of the moral view —"

> बृहस्पते अप तं वर्तया पथः सुगं नो अस्यै देववीतये कृधि ॥
> *bṛhaspate apa taṃ vartayā pathaḥ sugaṃ no asyai devavītaye kṛdhi ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-[?]-[?] [?], as read "२-३३-२" [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "Bṛhaspati, turn that path away; make for us an easy way for this divine feast".)*

"— in Ṛks such as this, the word *sugaṃ*, from the moral standpoint, means 'what is to be gone to well' (*suṣṭhu gantavyaṃ*): '*yajñānuṣṭhānāya sumatiṃ dehi*', 'give a good mind for the performance of sacrifice'; it is also understood as the good sense that performs sacrifice and the like. Moreover, in places such as 1-103-4 [?]; 6-109-2 [?], the word *sugaṃ* is explained as 'happiness'."

"Skandasvāmin explains this last sense as to be taken in this Ṛk also, saying *āsetitam api sukhanāmaitat; iha draṣṭavyaṃ* [read as printed, doubtful [?]; gloss, mine and tentative: 'this too is a name for happiness; to be seen here'], and cites the Ṛk —"

> अस्मभ्यमिन्द्र वरिवः सुगं कृधि प्र शत्रूणां मघवन् वृष्ण्या रुज ।
> *asmabhyam indra varivaḥ sugaṃ kṛdhi pra śatrūṇāṃ maghavan vṛṣṇyā ruja |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-102-4 [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "for us, Indra, make wide room and an easy way; break the vigour of the foes, bounteous one".)* "Having cited this Ṛk, they explain that, just as the sense is there, so here too the word *suga*, though not read among the names of happiness (*sukha*), has the meaning 'happiness'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 542)*

*vadhaiḥ* — root *han* (to strike, go); *ap* in the instrumental sense by *hanaś ca vadhaḥ* (Pā. 3-3-76 [?]); *vadha* as substitute for the root; the word ends in *a* and has the final acute; *ato lopaḥ* (as read) elides the *a* for the suffix *ap*…

### Page 542 (PDF 557)

*(Running head left: 542; centre: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 15 [?], Sūkta 94".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.9, continued from p. 541** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

*vadhaiḥ*, concluded: the suffix *ap* being *pit* is unaccented, and with the unaccented suffix's acute vowel dropped, *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* (Pā. 6-1-161 [?]) gives the acute to the suffix. — *duḥśaṃsān* — root *śaṃsu* (praise); with the word *duḥ* as upapada (in the sense of 'with difficulty'), *khal* in the passive by *īṣaddussuṣu* (Pā. 3-3-126 [?]); stem *duḥśaṃsa*; *liti* (Pā. 6-1-193 [?]): the syllable before the suffix, being *lit*, takes the acute; accusative plural *duḥśaṃsān*; with *āṭ*-type vowel following, *dīrghād aṭi samānapāde* (as read) gives *ru* for the *n*, and *āto 'ṭi nityam* (as read) gives nasalization of the preceding *ā*. — *jahi* — root *han* (striking, going); *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip* → *hi*; *hanter jaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-36 [?]) gives *ja*; because of *asiddhavad atrābhāt* (Pā. 6-4-22 [?]) the substitute is treated as not effected, so the elision of *hi* by *ato heḥ* does not take place; *nighāta* accent (following a tiṅanta, the verb as read). — *anti* — the word *antika*, with loss of the final *ka* by *kādilopo bahulam*. — *atriṇaḥ* — root *ad* (eating); *trin* by *ādeś ca ni ca* (Uṇ. 4-[?] [?], as read "४-५३७" [?]); the *i* after *n* is read in the suffix to prevent loss of the *n* (it would be elided as final by *halantyam* [as read]), so the stem *atrin*; nominative plural *atriṇaḥ*; the *i* acute by the suffix accent. — *gṛṇate* — root *gṝ* here in the sense of praise; *śatṛ* in the present sense; *śnā* by *kryādibhyaḥ śnā*; *sārvadhātukam apit* makes the suffix *ṅit*-like; *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. 6-4-112 [?]) elides the *ā* of *śnā*; *gṛṇat*; dative singular; with no *num*, the case-ending is acute by *śatur anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. 6-1-173 [?]). — *sugam* — root *gam* (going), with *su* as upapada, *ḍa* in the locative-type sense by *sudurorādhikaraṇe* (Pā. 3-2-48 [?]); *ḍit*-ness elides the *ṭi* of the root; stem *suga*; suffix accent; accusative singular. — *kṛdhi* — root *ḍukṛñ* (making); *loṭ* second person singular, *sip* → *hi*; *dhi* by *śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi* (Pā. 6-4-102 [?]); the *vikaraṇa* elided by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *nighāta* accent. ‖ 9 ‖ *(Grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numerals small and doubtful [?].)*

### Sūkta 94, Rik 10 (printed pp. 543–?)

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.10)** *(Jagatī; accent marks printed here, not reproduced)*

> यदयुक्था अरुषा रोहिता रथे वातजूता वृषभस्येव ते रवः ।
> आदिन्वसि वनिनो धूमकेतुनाग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ १० ॥

*yad ayukthā aruṣā rohitā rathe vātajūtā vṛṣabhasyeva te ravaḥ | ād invasi vanino dhūmaketunāgne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.10)**

> यत् । अयुक्थाः । अरुषा । रोहिता । रथे । वातऽजूता । वृषभस्यऽइव । ते । रवः ।
> आत् । इन्वसि । वनिनः । धूमऽकेतुना । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ १० ॥

*yat | ayukthāḥ | aruṣā | rohitā | rathe | vāta-jūtā | vṛṣabhasya-iva | te | ravaḥ | āt | invasi | vaninaḥ | dhūma-ketunā | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 10 ‖*

*(Reading note: the Pada, as printed, has* ād invasi *as* āt | invasi*, and the Saṃhitā* ayukthā *for the Pada's* ayukthāḥ *by sandhi, and* aruṣā rohitā *as printed in the dual.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.10)**

> हे अग्ने अरुषा आरोचमानौ रोहिता लोहितवर्णौ । रोहिते इत्यग्नेरश्वस्याख्या । रोहितोऽग्नेरिति दर्शनात् । रोहितेन त्वाग्निर्देवताां गमयेतु [?] । तै. सं. १-६-४-३ [?] इति मन्त्रवर्णात् । एते वै देवाश्वाः । तै. सं. १-६-४-३ [?] इति हि तत्र व्याख्यातं । वातजूता वातस्य वायोर्जूतं जवो वेग इव वेगो ययोस्तौ । ईदृशावश्वौ रथे यद्यदायुक्थाः अयोजयः तदानीं वनानि दहतस्ते तव रवः शब्दो वृषभस्येव दृप्तस्य महोक्षस्य शब्द इव गम्भीरो भवति । आदनन्तरं वनिनो वनसंबद्धान् वृक्षान् धूमकेतुना धूमः केतुः प्रज्ञापको यस्य तादृशेन रश्मिनेन्वसि [?] व्याप्नोषि । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ अयुक्थाः । युजिर् योगे । लुङि रुलो रुलीति सकारलोपः [?] । अरुषेत्यादिद्विवचनेषु सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । रवः । रु शब्दे । ऋदोरबिति भावेऽप् । इन्वसि । इवि व्याप्तौ । भ्वादिकः । इदित्त्वान्नुम् ॥

*he agne aruṣā ārocamānau rohitā lohitavarṇau | rohite ity agner aśvasyākhyā | rohito 'gner iti darśanāt | rohitena tvāgnir devatāṃ gamayetu [?] | tai. saṃ. 1-6-4-3 [?] iti mantravarṇāt | ete vai devāśvāḥ | tai. saṃ. 1-6-4-3 [?] iti hi tatra vyākhyātaṃ | vātajūtā vātasya vāyor jūtaṃ javo vega iva vego yayos tau | īdṛśāv aśvau rathe yad yad āyukthāḥ ayojayaḥ tadānīṃ vanāni dahatas te tava ravaḥ śabdo vṛṣabhasyeva dṛptasya mahokṣasya śabda iva gambhīro bhavati | ād anantaraṃ vanino vanasaṃbaddhān vṛkṣān dhūmaketunā dhūmaḥ ketuḥ prajñāpako yasya tādṛśena raśminenvasi [?] vyāpnoṣi | anyat pūrvavat ‖ ayukthāḥ | yujir yoge | luṅi rulo rulīti sakāralopaḥ [?] | aruṣety ādidvivaceṣu supāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ | ravaḥ | ru śabde | ṛdor ap iti bhāve 'p | invasi | ivi vyāptau | bhvādikaḥ | idittvān num ‖*

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "O Agni, the two shining (*aruṣā*), red (*rohitā*, 'red-coloured') [horses]. *Rohitā* is a name of the horses of Agni, as seen in the saying 'the *rohita* of Agni'; and in the mantra-wording 'Agni, with the *rohita*, may he bring you to the deity' (Taittirīya Saṃhitā, as read 1-6-4-3 [?]); 'these are the gods' horses' — so it is explained there. *vātajūtā* — those two whose speed (*jūta*) is like the speed (*vega*) of the wind. When you have yoked such a pair to your chariot, then, burning the forests, your roar is deep like the roar of a proud great bull. And after that, with a banner of smoke — that is, the smoke is the *ketu* (the sign) of him — you pervade the trees that belong to the forest. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: *ayukthāḥ* — *yuj* (joining) in the aorist, with elision of the *s* as printed [?]; *aruṣā* — the dual case-ending is replaced by *ā* by *supāṃ suluk…*; *ravaḥ* — root *ru* (sound), *ap* in the sense of the action by *ṛdor ap*; *invasi* — root *ivi* (pervading), class *bhvādi*, the *i*-marker gives *num*. *(The bhāṣya is clotted at the Taittirīya Saṃhitā quotation* rohitena tvāgnir devatāṃ gamayetu *and its two numerals; at* raśminenvasi*; and at the aorist elision clause; marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*agne* — O Agni; *aruṣā* — shining; *rohitā* — golden-coloured; *vātajūtā* — wind-swift; (your) horses [Kannada: *kuduregaḷu*]; *rathe* — to the chariot; *yat* — when; *ayukthāḥ* — are yoked (then); *te* — (forest-burning) your; *ravaḥ* — sound; *vṛṣabhasyeva* — like the bellow of a bull (is deep); *āt* — after that; *vaninaḥ* — all the trees in the forest; *dhūmaketunā* — with the flame made known by a banner-like smoke; *invasi* — you envelop; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayaṃ* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer harm."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Agni, as soon as you yoke to your chariot your shining, golden-hued, wind-swift horses, your roar, as you burn the forest, is deep like the bellow of a bull. After that you envelop all the trees in the forest with a flame that has the smoke for its banner. Through friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> When you have yoked the bright red horses, swift as the wind to your car, your roar is like that of a bull, and you envelope [sic] the forest trees with a banner of smoke ; Agni, let us not suffer injury, through your friendship.

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 31 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 545; foot: printer's signature "35 … Volume 7".)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.10 (Kannada)**

***aruṣā*** — "Although the word *aruṣa* has the ordinary sense 'reddish-brown', here, since the epithet *rohitā* is also present, it has been explained as 'shining' (*prakāśamāna*)."

***rohitā*** — "*rohito 'gneḥ* (Ni. 2-28 [?], as read) — the Nirukta-author thus gives the form of Agni's horse: 'golden-coloured', that is the sense."

***vātajūtā*** — *vātasya vāyoḥ jūtaṃ javaḥ vega iva vego yayoḥ tau*: "'Horses whose speed is like the speed of the wind'; here the word *vātajūta* is an epithet of Agni's horses. In some places it is also used as an epithet of Agni himself:"

> वि वातजूतो अतसेषु तिष्ठते वृथा जुहूभिः सृण्या तुविष्वणिः ।
> *vi vātajūto atiseṣu tiṣṭhate vṛthā juhūbhiḥ sṛṇyā tuviṣvaṇiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-58-5 as read [?])

*(The print's word before* tiṣṭhate *is read* atiseṣu *as printed, and is the Kannada-script reading of* atasesu*; doubtful [?]. Gloss, mine and tentative: "wind-driven, he stands apart among the bushes, with ladles, with the sickle, loud in sound".)*

> यद्वातजूतो वना व्यस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः ।
> *yad vātajūto vanā vy asthād agnir ha dāti romā pṛthivyāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-65-4 as read [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "when, wind-driven, he spread through the forests, Agni shears the hair of the earth".)* "In places such as these, the word is an epithet of Agni, meaning 'Agni urged on by the wind (*vātena preritaḥ*)'."

***vaninaḥ*** — *vanasaṃbaddhān vṛkṣān*: "the trees belonging to the forest."

***invasi*** — "*invati, nakṣati* and so on, ten [words] being read among the roots that mean 'pervasion' (Ni. 2-10 [?]); so *invasi* means 'you pervade'."

***dhūmaketunā*** — "They explain the word *dhūmaketu* in two ways. *Ketuḥ patākākāraḥ*; *ketuḥ patākāsthānīyo yasya saḥ*: '*ketu* means a standard (*dhvaja*); one whose banner is the smoke' — thus Agni, in one way; or, *ketuḥ jñānaṃ vā*: '*ketu* means knowledge' — 'one who is known by the smoke' (*dhūmena yaḥ jñāyate sa iti vā*) — in another way. The commentators explain it thus."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.10** *(grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 546)*

*ayukthāḥ* — root *yujir* (joining), *luṅ* second person singular, *thās*; *cleḥ siṅ/sic* in place of *cli*; *jhalo jhali* (Pā. 8-2-26 [?]) elides the *s*; *co kuḥ* (Pā. 8-2-30 [?]) turns *j* to *g* by *kutva*; *khari ca* (Pā. 8-4-55 [?]) turns *g* to *k* …

### Page 546 (PDF 561)

*(Running head left: 546; centre: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 15 [?], Sūkta 94".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.10, continued** *(grammar, noted briefly)*: *ayukthāḥ* — … *g* turns to *k*; because the word is connected with *yad*, the *nighāta* accent does not arise; since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the word has acute on its first syllable. — *aruṣā* — *aruṣā*, *rohitā*, *vātajūtā*: these dual forms with the dual ending following, the case-ending becomes *ā* by *supāṃ suluk…*. — *ravaḥ* — root *ru* (sound); *ap* in the sense of the action by *ṛdor ap*; guṇa of the root by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* and *av*-substitution; since *ap* is *pit*, it is unaccented and the root's accent remains. — *invasi* — root *ivi* (pervading), *bhvādi* class; *num* augment by *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. 7-1-58 [?]); *śap* as *vikaraṇa*; *laṭ* second person singular *sip*; *nighāta* accent, since it follows a tiṅanta (the printed *atijanta*, as read). — *vaninaḥ* — "that which has a forest (*vana*)": the suffix *ini* in the sense of possession by *ato 'ni ṭhanau* (as read); stem *vanin*; accusative plural *vaninaḥ*; the *i* acute by the suffix accent. ‖ 10 ‖ *(Grammar page, noted briefly; the sūtra numerals are small and doubtful [?].)*

*(Reading note: Saṃhitā* adha *and Pada* adha*, Saṃhitā* bibhyuḥ *and Pada* bibhyuḥ*; the Saṃhitā's compound* yavasādo *is divided in the Pada as* yavasa-adaḥ*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.11)**

> हे अग्ने अध दग्धुं वनप्रवेशानन्तरं स्वनात्त्वदीयोत्पूर्वोत्कृष्टगम्भीरशब्दात् । उतशब्दोऽप्यर्थः । पतत्रिणः पक्षिणोऽपि बिभ्युः । बिभ्यति भयं प्राप्नुवन्ति । उत्पतनेन देशान्तरं गन्तुं समर्थाः पक्षिणोऽपि यदा भयं प्राप्नुवन्ति किमु वक्तव्यमन्येषां तत्रत्यानां वृकादीनां भीतिर्जायत इति । अतस्त्वयि वनं प्रविशति सर्वे प्राणिनो भयं प्राप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः । तादृशस्य ते तव द्रप्साः ज्वालैकदेशा यवसादो यवसानामत्तारः संकोचयद्यदा [?] व्यस्थिरन् विविधमवतिष्ठन्ते तत्तदा ते तव सर्वमरण्यं सुगं सुखेन गन्तुं शक्यं । अतस्तावकेभ्यस्त्वदीयेभ्यो रथेभ्यश्च तदरण्यं सुगं भवति । पूर्वं प्रवृत्तैर्ज्वालाग्रैस्तृणादिषु दग्धेषु सत्सु त्वदीया रथाः प्रतिबन्धमन्तरेण पश्चाद्गच्छन्तीति भावः । अन्यत्समानं ॥ बिभ्युः । ञिभी भये । छान्दसो लिट् । एरनेकाच इति यण् । व्यस्थिरन् । समवप्रविभ्यः स्थ इति तिष्ठतेरात्मनेपदं । लुङः व्यत्ययेन झस्य रन् । स्थाघ्वोरिच्चेतीत्त्वं । प्रस्पादङ्गात् [?] । पा. ८-३-१२ [?] इति सलोपः । तावकेभ्यः । तवकममकावेकवचने । पा. सू. ४-३-३ [?] इति युष्मदस्तवकादेशः ॥

*he agne adha dagdhuṃ vanapraveśānantaraṃ svanāt tvadīyotpūrvotkṛṣṭagambhīraśabdāt | utaśabdo 'py arthaḥ | patatriṇaḥ pakṣiṇo 'pi bibhyuḥ | bibhyati bhayaṃ prāpnuvanti | utpatanena deśāntaraṃ gantuṃ samarthāḥ pakṣiṇo 'pi yadā bhayaṃ prāpnuvanti kimu vaktavyam anyeṣāṃ tatratyānāṃ vṛkādīnāṃ bhītir jāyata iti | atas tvayi vanaṃ praviśati sarve prāṇino bhayaṃ prāpnuvantīty arthaḥ | tādṛśasya te tava drapsāḥ jvālaikadeśā yavasādo yavasānām attāraḥ saṃkocayad yadā [?] vyasthiran vividham avatiṣṭhante tat tadā te tava sarvam araṇyaṃ sugaṃ sukhena gantuṃ śakyaṃ | atas tāvakebhyas tvadīyebhyo rathebhyaś ca tad araṇyaṃ sugaṃ bhavati | pūrvaṃ pravṛttair jvālāgrais tṛṇādiṣu dagdheṣu satsu tvadīyā rathāḥ pratibandham antareṇa paścād gacchantīti bhāvaḥ | anyat samānaṃ ‖ bibhyuḥ | ñibhī bhaye | chāndaso liṭ | eranekāca iti yaṇ | vyasthiran | samavaprabhyaḥ stha iti tiṣṭhater ātmanepadaṃ | luṅaḥ vyatyayena jhasya ran | sthāghvor ic ceti ittvaṃ | prasvādaṅgāt [?] | pā. 8-3-12 [?] iti salopaḥ | tāvakebhyaḥ | tavakamamakāv ekavacane | pā. sū. 4-3-3 [?] iti yuṣmadas tavakādeśaḥ ‖*

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "O Agni, *adha* — after your entering the forest to burn it — *svanāt*, from your loud, deep roar (*uta* here has the sense 'even'): the winged ones (*patatriṇaḥ*), the birds also, are afraid. If even birds, able to go to another place by flying up, are afraid, what is to be said of the fear that arises in the other creatures there, the wolves and the like? So the sense is that when you enter the forest, all creatures fall into fear. When your sparks (*drapsāḥ* — portions of flame), the eaters of grass (*yavasādaḥ*), spread out in many ways, then for you the whole forest is easy to travel (*sugam*): so that forest becomes easy for your chariots also. The sense is that when the grass and the like have been burned by the flame-tips that spread first, your chariots follow after without obstruction. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: *bibhyuḥ* — *ñibhī* (fear), the Vedic perfect, with *y* for the vowel by *eranekāca…*; *vyasthiran* — the *ātmanepada* of *sthā* after *sam, ava, pra, vi* by the rule on *sthā*; *ran* in place of *jhi* by the transposition of terms in the *luṅ*; *i* for the root vowel by *sthāghvor ic ca*; elision of *s* [clotted, the rule's wording and number doubtful [?]]; *tāvakebhyaḥ* — *tavaka* as substitute for *yuṣmad* in the singular (the rule number doubtful [?]). *(The bhāṣya is clotted at* saṃkocayad yadā *and at* prasvādaṅgāt*; marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)** *(begun at the foot of p. 547; continues on p. 548)*

"*agne* — O Agni; *atha* — after you have entered the forest; *svanāt* — (by your) sound; *patatriṇaḥ uta* — even the birds; *bibhyuḥ* — are afraid; *te* — your; *drapsāḥ* — the parts of flame; *yavasādaḥ* — burning up all the grass; *yat* — when; *vyasthiran* — they spread in all directions; *tat* — then; *te* — to you; *sugaṃ* — (all the forest) it becomes possible to enter easily; *tāvakebhyaḥ* — your; *rathebhyaḥ* — for the chariots also (it is possible to enter easily…"

### Page 548 (PDF 563)

*(Running head left: 548; centre: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 15 [?], Sūkta 94".)*

**Pratipadārtha of Rik 94.11, concluded from p. 547:** "…(it is possible to enter easily) — it becomes [so]; *tava* — your; *sakhye* — through friendship; *vayaṃ* — we; *mā riṣāma* — may we not suffer (any) harm."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Agni, as soon as you have entered the forest, even the birds are afraid at your roar. When the portions of your flame, burning up all the grass, spread in all directions, the entry of the forest becomes very easy for you and for your chariots. Through friendship with you, may we suffer no harm of any kind."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> At your roaring even the birds are terrified ; when your flames, consuming the grass, have spread in all directions, (the wood) is easy of access to you and to your chariots ; Agni, let us not suffer injury through your friendship.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 94.11 (Kannada)**

***drapsāḥ*** — "The word *drapsa* ordinarily means 'that which flows' (*dravaṇa-śīla*), that is, 'what is to be run, flowing', or it has been used in the sense 'the drops of Soma-juice, like water-drops'. But in some contexts it means 'a ray of Agni', 'a banner', 'the moon'. For the word *drapsāḥ* in this Ṛk they explain *jvālaikadeśāḥ*, 'portions of the flame'. Skandasvāmin takes it as *drapsaśabdaḥ kaṭhinavacanaḥ kaṭhināḥ bahularūpāḥ* [as read, doubtful [?]]: 'the word *drapsa* gives the meaning "hard"', and says it is to be understood here as the hard and abundant flame of Agni."

***vyasthiran*** — *tiṣṭheḥ idaṃ rūpaṃ | vitiṣṭhante | sarvaṃ vyāpnuvantīty arthaḥ*: "'this is a form of *sthā*: they stand in various ways, they pervade everything' — that is the sense: 'occupy all', or 'pervade'. The flame of Agni pervades everything and spreads."

***sugaṃ*** — "The various senses of this word have been given already, in explaining the 9th Ṛk of this very Sūkta."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.11** *(grammar page, noted briefly; continues on p. 549)*

*adha* — in the word *atha* the *tha* becomes *dha* by Vedic variation. — *bibhyuḥ* — root *ñibhī* (fear); in the present sense, *liṭ* by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*; reduplication of the root; the reduplicate takes *jaś* (the *bh* → *b*); third person plural *jhi* → *us*; *asaṃyogāl liṭ kit*… *(continues on p. 549)*

### Page 549 (PDF 564)

*(Running head left: "A. 1 A. 6 Va. 31 [?]"; centre: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right: 549.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 94.11, continued** *(grammar, noted briefly)*: *bibhyuḥ* — … by *asaṃyogāl liṭ kit* (Pā. 1-2-5 [?]) it is *kit*, so the root takes no *guṇa*; *eranekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya* (Pā. 6-4-82 [?]) turns the *i* to *y*; *nighāta* accent, following a tiṅanta. — *vyasthiran* — root *ṣṭhā* (cessation of motion), usually parasmaipada, but by *samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ* (Pā. 1-3-22 [?]) it takes the *ātmanepada*; *luṅ*, third person plural, *jha*; by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. 3-1-85 [?]) *ran* replaces *jha*; *sthāghvor ic ca* (Pā. 1-2-17 [?]) gives *i* for the root's vowel in *luṅ*; then, the *sic* following a short vowel being elided by *hrasvād aṅgāt* (Pā. 8-2-27 [?]) — the print's clotted *prasvādaṅgāt* of the bhāṣya (p. 547) is to be read *hrasvād aṅgāt*, with the number as read here, not the 8-3-12 of the bhāṣya's tail [?]; the augment *aṭ* for the stem. Because the word *yat* stands before it, the *nighāta* accent is blocked by *yadvṛttān nityam* (as read); as the augment *aṭ* is acute, the first syllable is acute. — *tāvakebhyaḥ* — "these (are) yours": *tava ime tāvakāḥ*, in the sense of relationship; by *yuṣmadasmador anyatarasyāṃ khañ ca* (as read) the suffix *aṇ* follows; with that suffix following, *tavakamamakāv ekavacane* (Pā. 4-3-3 [?]) gives *tavaka* for *yuṣmad*; *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ* gives *vṛddhi* of the first vowel; the suffix accent falls on the last syllable; the form is the dative plural. ‖ 11 ‖ *(Grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numerals small and doubtful [?].)*

### Sūkta 94, Rik 12 (printed pp. 549–?)

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 94.12)** *(Jagatī; accent marks printed here, not reproduced)*

> अयं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धायसेऽवयातां मरुतां हेळो अद्भुतः ।
> मृळा सु नो भूत्वेषां मनः पुनरग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥ १२ ॥

*ayaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya dhāyase 'vayātāṃ marutāṃ heḷo adbhutaḥ | mṛḷā su no bhūtv eṣāṃ manaḥ punar agne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖ 12 ‖*

### Page 550 (PDF 565)

*(Running head left: 550; centre: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right: "Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 15 [?], Sūkta 94".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 94.12)**

> अयम् । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । धायसे । अवऽयाताम् । मरुताम् । हेळः । अद्भुतः ।
> मृळ । सु । नः । भूतु । एषाम् । मनः । अग्ने । सख्ये । मा । रिषाम । वयम् । तव ॥ १२ ॥

*ayam | mitrasya | varuṇasya | dhāyase | ava-yātām | marutām | heḷaḥ | adbhutaḥ | mṛḷa | su | naḥ | bhūtu | eṣām | manaḥ | agne | sakhye | mā | riṣāma | vayam | tava ‖ 12 ‖*

*(Reading note: the Pada line as printed, checked on an enlargement, has no* punaḥ *between* manaḥ *and* agne*, although the Saṃhitā has* punar agne*; the omission is the print's. The Saṃhitā's* mṛḷā *is the Pada's* mṛḷa*, and* bhūtv eṣām *is* bhūtu | eṣām*.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 94.12)**

> अयमग्नेः स्तोता मित्रस्याहरभिमानिनो देवस्य वरुणस्य रात्र्यभिमानिनश्च संबन्धिने धायसे धारणायोवस्थापनाय [?] भवतु । मित्रावरुणाविममग्नेः स्तोतारं धारयितामित्यर्थः । अवयातामवस्ताद् गच्छतां स्वर्गलोकस्याधस्तादन्तरिक्षे वर्तमानानां मरुतामेतन्नामकानां देवानां हेळः क्रोधो ऽद्भुतो महान् भवति । अद्भुत इत्येतन्महन्नाम । तस्मात्क्रोधादिममग्नेः स्तोतारं मित्रावरुणौ रक्षतामिति शेषः । असि च नोऽस्मान् हे अग्ने सु मृळ सुष्ठु मृडय । सुखय । एषां मरुतां मनश्च पुनर्भूतु । पुनरपि प्रसन्नं भवतु । अन्यत्समानं ॥ धायसे । वहिहाधाङ्भ्यश्छन्दसीति भावेऽसुन् । णिदित्यनुवृत्तेरातो युक् चिण्कृतोरिति युक् । अवयातां । या प्रापणे । अस्मादेवपूर्वाल्लटः शतृ । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । मृळ । मृड सुखने । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाज्ञेरनिटीति णिलोपः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । भूतु । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् ॥

*ayam agneḥ stotā mitrasyāhar-abhimāninā devasya varuṇasya rātry-abhimāninaś ca saṃbandhine dhāyase dhāraṇāyovasthāpanāya [?] bhavatu | mitrāvaruṇāv imam agneḥ stotāraṃ dhārayitām ity arthaḥ | avayātām avastād gacchatāṃ svargalokasyādhastād antarikṣe vartamānānāṃ marutām etannāmakānāṃ devānāṃ heḷaḥ krodho 'dbhuto mahān bhavati | adbhuta ity etan mahannāma | tasmāt krodhād imam agneḥ stotāraṃ mitrāvaruṇau rakṣatām iti śeṣaḥ | asi ca no 'smān he agne su mṛḷa suṣṭhu mṛḍaya | sukhaya | eṣāṃ marutāṃ manaś ca punar bhūtu | punar api prasannaṃ bhavatu | anyat samānaṃ ‖ dhāyase | vahihādhāṅbhyaś chandasīti bhāve 'sun | ṇid ity anuvṛtter āto yuk ciṇkṛtor iti yuk | avayātāṃ | yā prāpaṇe | asmād eva pūrvāl laṭaḥ śatṛ | śatur anuma iti vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | mṛḷa | mṛḍa sukhane | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāj ñer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | dvyaco 'tas tiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | bhūtu | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk ‖*

*(The print's* asi ca no 'smān *is read as printed, where the sense requires* kṛdhi *or the like — it is presumably a misprint for* asmān *alone; also the opening clause* asi ca nosmān *[?]. The sūtras are named without numbers in this tail; none supplied.)*

*Gloss (mine, from the Kannada and the bhāṣya as printed):* "May this praiser of Agni be [fit] for the support (*dhāyase*) belonging to Mitra, the god who presides over the day, and Varuṇa, who presides over the night: that is, may Mitra and Varuṇa sustain this praiser of Agni. The anger (*heḷaḥ*) of the Maruts, the gods so named, who dwell in the atmosphere below the world of heaven (*avayātām* — 'those who go below'), is *adbhuta*, great; (*adbhuta* is a word for 'great'); from that anger may Mitra and Varuṇa protect this praiser of Agni, so the sentence is completed. And, O Agni, *su mṛḷa*, make us well content; and let the mind of these Maruts be again [kindly], let it become gracious once more. The rest as before." Grammatical tail: *dhāyase* — the suffix *asun* in the sense of the action after the roots *vah, hā, dhā* and the like in the Veda, with the augment *yuk*; *avayātām* — *yā* (reaching), *śatṛ* in the present of that root with the prefix *ava*, with the case-ending acute by the rule on *śatṛ*; *mṛḷa* — *mṛḍa* (pleasing); *śap* taken as *ārdhadhātuka*, with *ṇi*-elision; lengthening in the Saṃhitā (*mṛḷā*); *bhūtu* — elision of *śap* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*. *(The bhāṣya is clotted at* dhāraṇāyovasthāpanāya*; marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)** *(begun at the foot of p. 550; continues on p. 551)*

"*ayaṃ* — this sacrificer (who praises Agni); *mitrasya* — of Mitra (who presides over the day); *varuṇasya* — and of Varuṇa (who presides over the night); *dhāyase* — to obtain support (the Kannada word, as read, doubtful [?]) (fit); *avayātāṃ* — those who move below (in the lower region of the world of heaven); *marutāṃ* — of the Maruts; *heḷaḥ* — anger; *adbhutaḥ* — is great (may this sacrificer who praises Agni be protected by Mitra and Varuṇa from this anger); *agne* — O Agni; *naḥ* — us; *sumṛḷa* — make well content; *eṣāṃ* — of these Maruts; *manaḥ* — the mind; *punaḥ* — …"
